aliyas-journal-143.excerpt: Compare a JVC studio and one-bedroom apartment using full acquisition cost, tenant fit, owner expenses and net rental income.
aliyas-journal-143.introduction:
A Jumeirah Village Circle studio may require less capital than a one-bedroom apartment in a particular comparison, but the lower price does not automatically produce the better investment. Compare real units in similar buildings on the total amount invested, achievable rent, vacancy, service charges and likely resale alternatives.

The calculations below use sample figures to demonstrate the method. Use the worked comparison to see how purchase cost and annual income affect each investment.
takeaways: Compare actual units on the same cost, rent and vacancy assumptions rather than bedroom count alone.
A one-bedroom's extra net income should be considered against the additional capital required.
Check the building's approved service charges, condition, tenant demand and competing supply.

sections.heading: What should the comparison include?
sections.body:
Select a studio and one-bedroom apartment with comparable condition, completion status and access to services. Record usable layout, floor, parking, furnishing, cooling, view and building facilities. A large studio may compete differently from a small one-bedroom; a label alone does not describe the home.

[Property Finder's JVC area guide](https://www.propertyfinder.ae/en/area-insights/dubai/jumeirah-village-circle) provides neighbourhood context. Visit the exact building and test routes to the places your intended tenant might use. The [JVC and Arjan comparison](/journal/jvc-vs-arjan-apartment-investment-comparison) explains how to assess the wider location and competing supply.

Seek recent signed leases for similar units in the same building if available, and record their date and terms. An advertised rent is useful context but is not proof of what was agreed or collected.

Confirm whether parking and storage are included, because these features affect how a tenant uses either layout.

table.caption: Studio and one-bedroom comparison worksheet
rows: Price plus all buyer and setup costs
Price plus all buyer and setup costs

sections.heading: Work through a worked example
sections.body:
Assume a studio requires AED 800,000 of total acquisition cost and produces AED 44,000 in annual net operating income after vacancy and owner costs. Its net operating yield is 5.5%. Assume a one-bedroom requires AED 1,100,000 and produces AED 55,000 net, or 5%. Both figures are worked examples before finance, tax and the costs associated with a sale.

The one-bedroom requires AED 300,000 more capital and produces AED 11,000 more annual net income under these assumptions. That incremental income divided by incremental capital is approximately 3.67%. The comparison focuses on annual income after the stated operating costs.

The chart shows the two sample net yields. Change the inputs to reflect the actual apartments and test a longer vacancy or repair.

chart.title: Example net operating yield by unit type
chart.note: Example inputs; returns are shown before financing, tax and the costs associated with a sale.

sections.heading: Check costs and the denominator
sections.body:
Add the purchase price, buyer-paid registration and brokerage, applicable tax on services, initial repairs and furnishing. Request written quotes. A smaller unit can still have meaningful fixed transaction costs, so compare the full capital invested rather than the advertised price alone.

Dubai Land Department's [service charge index](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/service-charge-index/) helps check approved community charges. Request the current unit statement, area basis and arrears from management. Add owner-paid management, repairs and insurance, and keep a vacancy allowance.

The [Dubai net rental yield guide](/journal/how-to-calculate-net-rental-yield-in-dubai) shows the formula. Keep mortgage payments and the outstanding loan in a separate cash-flow schedule so the operating comparison remains consistent.

sections.heading: Consider the tenant and the building
sections.body:
Ask whether the layout suits the household likely to rent it: storage, working space, kitchen, privacy and parking can matter as much as the bedroom label. Inspect shared areas and ask about maintenance, access control, lifts and the actual facilities. Check the route to work, transport and daily services at useful times.

Review current competing units and nearby scheduled handovers. A large number of similar apartments may affect the time needed to let, but future vacancy cannot be inferred from a development count alone. Ask how long comparable homes have been offered and seek evidence of signed leases.

If the property is off-plan, verify the project and contract and allow for delivery risk. A future rental estimate is not income until the unit is usable and let.

sections.heading: Test the exit and downside
sections.body:
Look for recent completed sales of similar studios and one-bedroom units where available. Record the dates, condition and terms, and separate completed transactions from asking prices. Include selling charges and any outstanding loan in a future cash estimate.

Test a lower rent, higher service charge and longer vacancy for each unit. The one-bedroom's higher assumed income may or may not compensate for the additional capital; the answer changes with actual price and costs. Keep a reserve for repairs and periods without a tenant.

Assess rental yield alongside selling costs and changes in the property’s value over the holding period. Review your time horizon and ability to absorb a less favourable outcome.

sections.heading: Check financing and the cash reserve
sections.body:
If you intend to borrow, request a written offer for each property showing the loan amount, valuation, rate, fees, insurance and repayment schedule. A bank may assess the two apartments differently, so a comparison based on equal financing assumptions should be updated once actual offers are available. Separate principal and interest and track the remaining balance at a possible sale.

Keep enough cash for payments, repairs and vacancy. Consider whether the larger capital commitment to a one-bedroom leaves sufficient flexibility for other obligations. A higher projected income is useful only if the investor can sustain the property through a less favourable period.

sections.heading: Request current JVC options
sections.body:
Browse the [Aliyas JVC project collection](/projects?emirate=Dubai&area=dubai-jvc) and [contact Aliyas](/contact) with your budget and preferred unit type. Ask which exact apartments are currently available and request their plans, price, service charges and terms.

Verify ownership and official transaction requirements before committing, and replace the example with unit-specific evidence.

aliyas-journal-144.excerpt: Compare Jumeirah Village Circle and Arjan apartment investments using the building, tenant needs, acquisition cost, service charges and net rent.
aliyas-journal-144.introduction:
Jumeirah Village Circle (JVC) and Arjan are both Dubai apartment markets worth comparing at the level of an individual building and unit. The choice depends on what you pay, the lease evidence, service charges, future competition and the way a tenant uses the location. An area-wide advertised yield cannot decide the investment for you.

This guide sets out a like-for-like method. The figures below provide a worked comparison of purchase costs and annual income in two scenarios.
takeaways: Compare the precise building, layout, parking and route to the tenant's likely destinations.
Use recent comparable leases and the unit's approved service charges to estimate net income.
Check ownership, project registration, construction and competing supply before committing.

sections.heading: Understand the two locations
sections.body:
[Property Finder's JVC guide](https://www.propertyfinder.ae/en/area-insights/dubai/jumeirah-village-circle) describes a community with apartments and a mix of other homes, parks and retail. Its [Arjan guide](https://www.propertyfinder.ae/en/area-insights/dubai/arjan) describes a mixed-use area with residential buildings near Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road and Umm Suqeim Road. These descriptions provide context; they do not establish the condition or performance of a specific tower.

Visit the exact addresses, check the entrance and parking, and test routes at times the intended tenant would travel. Ask about nearby construction, shops and access to public transport. A building's position and management may matter more than a broad neighbourhood description.

The [Dubai market guide](/journal/dubai-property-market-2026) provides wider context for comparing alternatives, while this guide focuses on JVC and Arjan.

table.caption: JVC and Arjan: property-level comparison
rows: Inspect the unit, parking and actual routes
Inspect the unit, parking and actual routes
Seek recent signed leases in the building
Check approved charges and repair history
Check approved charges and repair history

sections.heading: Inspect the building and likely tenant fit
sections.body:
Identify the apartment's usable layout, bedroom size, storage, noise, cooling and the condition of the common areas. Check the allocated parking and the actual facilities rather than relying on a project-wide advertisement. For an off-plan apartment, review the contracted specifications, floor plan, payment milestones and handover provisions.

Consider the likely tenant's work, school and daily travel. Ask whether public transport and nearby services work from the specific building. A short distance on a map can involve a different route or junction in practice. Test the journey and record what is open today rather than assuming a planned amenity has been completed.

Look at comparable rental supply in and around the building. More competing units can affect the time needed to let or the rent achieved, although the effect cannot be predicted from a project count alone.

sections.heading: Calculate total cost and service charges
sections.body:
Add the purchase price, registration and brokerage costs, financing fees where relevant, initial repairs and furnishing. Obtain a current written quotation for the specific transaction. Keep a separate reserve for vacancy and unexpected work. Compare apartments on the same financing basis.

Dubai Land Department's [service charge index](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/service-charge-index/) provides a way to check approved community service charges. Ask the management for the unit statement, applicable area basis, arrears and what services are included. A building's charge can differ from another in the same area.

For a ready unit, check title, seller authority, tenancy and any mortgage. For a new project, verify the registered project, developer, payment recipient and the agreement. Ask DLD to confirm the ownership right and process for your particular unit.

sections.heading: Compare net rental income
sections.body:
Suppose a sample JVC apartment requires AED 1,000,000 in total acquisition cost and yields AED 50,000 in annual net operating income after vacancy and owner costs. A sample Arjan alternative requires AED 900,000 and yields AED 43,200 net. Their respective net operating yields are 5% and 4.8%. These example figures show how to compare costs and yields using the same calculation for each home.

Use recent signed leases for apartments comparable in size, furnishing, parking and condition. Subtract vacancy, the owner's service charges, management, repairs and insurance from expected rent. Divide by the full acquisition cost; keep finance and sale costs separate.

The chart shows the example only. Test a lower rent or higher charge and do not infer that either neighbourhood is generally superior from two sample cases.

chart.title: Example annual net operating yield
chart.note: Sample assumptions; yields are before finance, tax and sale costs and do not represent area averages.

sections.heading: Test the exit and the unknowns
sections.body:
Look for recent completed sales of comparable apartments as well as current competing listings. Compare asking prices with recent completed sales and the terms of similar properties. Allow for selling costs, remaining loan and the possibility of a longer sale period.

Check how many nearby buildings are scheduled for handover and whether their units compete with yours. Scheduled supply may be delayed or altered; it is not proof of future vacancy or price changes. Inspect the developer's track record and the individual project's progress where available.

Write down the uncertainties that matter most and the evidence needed to resolve each one. A property that fails your budget, ownership or condition requirements should not qualify merely because an advertised yield looks attractive.

sections.heading: Check the payment timeline
sections.body:
For an off-plan unit, write every instalment date and the conditions attached to it, including the amount due at handover and any payments afterwards. Compare the schedule with your available cash and a possible delay. Ask the developer how construction progress is reported and verify the registered project and payment arrangements independently.

For a ready unit, include the timing of the deposit, loan approval if required and transfer charges. A similar headline price can require very different cash at different points. Do not count an expected future rental income until the apartment can legally be occupied and the costs of letting have been considered.

sections.heading: Explore current opportunities
sections.body:
Browse the [Aliyas JVC projects](/projects?emirate=Dubai&area=dubai-jvc) and [Arjan projects](/projects?emirate=Dubai&area=dubai-arjan), then ask which exact units are currently available. Request a plan, price, payment terms and current building charges for each option.

[Contact Aliyas](/contact) with your budget, intended tenant and holding period. Verify the project, official charges and ownership documents before making a commitment.

aliyas-journal-145.excerpt: Assess Dubai South property investment opportunities and risks through current infrastructure, project delivery, rental evidence and competing supply.
aliyas-journal-145.introduction:
Dubai South combines residential development with aviation and logistics activity, but a large infrastructure plan does not guarantee the performance of an individual apartment. Compare the exact project, current services, purchase cost, tenant demand and future competition before treating the area as an investment.

This guide separates official infrastructure announcements from assumptions about property returns. The worked numbers show how to compare the investment costs for two apartments.
takeaways: Distinguish announced airport expansion and long-term plans from facilities operating today.
Check the specific unit's registration, construction status, access, building costs and comparable leases.
Test vacancy, service charges, project delays and resale risk instead of assuming infrastructure guarantees gains.

sections.heading: What is the long-term infrastructure context?
sections.body:
Dubai's [Government Media Office announced in April 2024](https://mediaoffice.ae/en/news/2024/april/28-04/al-maktoum-international-airport) approval of designs for a new Al Maktoum International Airport passenger terminal, with an announced AED 128 billion cost and long-term capacity plans. These are plans for aviation infrastructure, not evidence of a return on a specific home.

In a [September 2026 media briefing](https://cd1.mediaoffice.ae/en/news/2026/september/11-09/dubai-airports-ceo-outlines-dxb-growth-and-future-of-dubai-aviation), Dubai Airports' chief executive said the first major phase was on track for the early 2030s. That is a stated outlook at the time, not an already completed facility or a guarantee that a particular property will appreciate.

Check the latest official progress and the exact route from the building. The [Dubai area comparison](/journal/jvc-vs-arjan-apartment-investment-comparison) provides a method for comparing a different location on unit-level evidence.

table.caption: Dubai South: opportunity and risk questions
rows: Current status, timing and actual building access
Possible tenants connected with nearby work
Recent signed leases and tenant requirements
Choice of plans and payment schedules
Different entry points across property types
Full cost, charges, finance and reserve

sections.heading: What is available to a resident today?
sections.body:
Dubai South's [Residential District update](https://www.dubaisouth.ae/en/newsroom/dubai-south-sells-out-south-living-project-confirms-huge-demand-for-spacious-units-in-the-area) describes existing amenities and residential development. As a developer source, it is useful for identifying facilities to verify, but project-specific availability and operating hours may change.

Visit the exact location and check roads, parking, shops, school access and public transport relevant to the intended tenant. Ask schools about admission and transport rather than assuming a place. Test travel at the time it would be used; a planned connection or headline journey time is not the same as current service from the building.

Inspect the apartment and common areas, or for off-plan request the contracted specification and dated construction evidence. A district description cannot establish the quality of one unit.

sections.heading: Test rent and owner costs
sections.body:
Use recent signed leases for comparable apartments, adjusting for size, condition, furnishing, parking and included services. Subtract vacancy and owner-paid service charges, management, repairs and insurance. Divide net operating income by full acquisition cost. The [Dubai net yield guide](/journal/how-to-calculate-net-rental-yield-in-dubai) explains the calculation.

For a sample property costing AED 1,000,000 in total, suppose one scenario has AED 70,000 rent and AED 20,000 in vacancy and owner costs, leaving AED 50,000 or 5%. A weaker scenario assumes AED 60,000 rent and AED 25,000 in vacancy and costs, leaving AED 35,000 or 3.5%. These example inputs show how the purchase cost and annual income fit into the calculation.

The chart compares the resulting annual income before finance, tax and sale costs. Neither scenario is a prediction or a guarantee.

chart.title: Example annual net operating income
chart.note: Sample assumptions on AED 1,000,000 total capital; financing, tax and sale costs are excluded.

sections.heading: Check project delivery and supply
sections.body:
For off-plan, verify the project and developer through DLD's [project status enquiry](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/real-estate-project-status-landing/real-estate-project-status/). Check the contract, payment recipient, initial registration, handover provisions and current progress. Keep sufficient cash for instalments even if the project or your plans are delayed.

Look at scheduled nearby handovers and the number and type of units that could compete for similar tenants. Future supply is a schedule, not proof that all units will be completed or vacant at the same time. Ask for evidence and update it as the project progresses.

A payment plan can change cash timing, but it does not by itself make the underlying purchase price attractive. Compare ready and off-plan alternatives on total cost and risk.

sections.heading: Assess the exit and holding period
sections.body:
Seek completed sales of genuinely similar properties where available and separate them from asking prices. Consider selling charges, any remaining loan and the time needed to find a buyer. An infrastructure announcement may influence expectations, but the timing and effect on a particular unit are uncertain.

Test a longer holding period, a lower rent and a sale price below the purchase price. Keep a reserve for repairs and periods without a tenant. If the investment works only when a projected airport milestone produces immediate growth, the plan is exposed to assumptions outside your control.

Verify the ownership right for the buyer, title or initial registration, building obligations and current official charges for the unit.

sections.heading: Check the building's ongoing obligations
sections.body:
Ask for the current service-charge statement or, for a new project, the estimate and basis of calculation. Confirm whether the figure is approved, which shared services it covers and when the final amount will be known. Include utility or cooling charges that the owner may have to pay while the unit is empty.

Review the developer's and building management's contact details, maintenance arrangements and any remaining payment obligations. A planned amenity may be valuable to a future tenant, but check whether it is part of the signed specification and whether it is operating. Keep those distinctions in the comparison.

sections.heading: Explore specific Dubai South projects
sections.body:
Browse the [Aliyas Dubai South project collection](/projects?emirate=Dubai&area=dubai-south) and ask which units are currently available. [Contact Aliyas](/contact) with your budget, intended tenant and holding period to request the exact plan, price, payment schedule and documents.

aliyas-journal-146.excerpt: Compare Business Bay and Dubai Marina rental investments by the actual unit, tenant access, service charges, net income and resale evidence.
aliyas-journal-146.introduction:
Business Bay and Dubai Marina offer different settings for a Dubai rental apartment, but neither neighbourhood guarantees a stronger return. The purchase price, building, access, tenant demand and owner costs of the exact unit determine the comparison. Use recent comparable leases and completed sales rather than relying only on an area-wide yield.

This guide sets out the checks and a sample calculation. The numbers form a worked example that can be adapted to the properties on your shortlist.
takeaways: Compare the building and intended tenant's daily routes as well as the area name.
Calculate net operating income after vacancy and owner expenses using the full acquisition cost.
Check service charges, short-term rental permissions if relevant, competing supply and exit costs.

sections.heading: How do the locations differ?
sections.body:
[Bayut's Business Bay guide](https://www.bayut.com/area-guides/business-bay/) describes a mixed-use district around the Dubai Water Canal, with residential and commercial buildings. [Emaar's Dubai Marina guide](https://www.emaar.com/en/our-communities/dubai-marina) describes a waterfront residential setting with a promenade and retail. These are broad descriptions; the location and condition of a tower can change a tenant's experience.

The [RTA station map](https://www.rta.ae/wps/portal/rta/ae/public-transport/metro-stations-map) lists Business Bay and stations serving the Marina/JLT corridor. Check the actual walking route and transport service from the building; an area being on a map does not mean every apartment is close to a station.

Visit each candidate at the time its intended tenant might travel and inspect parking, noise, shared facilities and nearby services. The [JVC and Arjan area comparison](/journal/jvc-vs-arjan-apartment-investment-comparison) offers another example of building-level comparison.

rows: Check the specific building's work and transport access
Check the specific building's work, transport and waterfront access
Compare recent signed leases in similar units
Compare recent signed leases in similar units
Request the unit's charge and repair history
Request the unit's charge and repair history

sections.heading: Compare net income on the same basis
sections.body:
Suppose a sample Business Bay apartment costs AED 2,000,000 including acquisition costs and produces AED 90,000 annual net operating income after vacancy and owner expenses. Its net yield is 4.5%. A sample Marina apartment costs AED 2,200,000 and produces AED 99,000 net, also 4.5%. These example figures show how annual income and purchase costs affect the yield calculation.

The same percentage can conceal different cash requirements, income and risks. The Marina example requires AED 200,000 more capital and produces AED 9,000 more annual net income under these assumptions. The chart compares those sample income amounts before finance, tax and sale costs.

Use actual signed leases and unit-specific charges, then test a lower rent, longer vacancy and unexpected repair. The [Dubai net yield guide](/journal/how-to-calculate-net-rental-yield-in-dubai) explains the formula.

chart.title: Example annual net operating income
chart.note: Sample inputs; each example yields 4.5% on its assumed total acquisition cost before finance, tax and sale costs.

sections.heading: Check costs and building condition
sections.body:
Add the price, registration and brokerage, any finance charges, initial work and furnishing to calculate total acquisition cost. Ask for written quotes and confirm who pays each fee. Keep a reserve for a vacant period and repairs.

Use DLD's [service charge index](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/service-charge-index/) and request the current statement for the unit. Check the approved rate, area basis, arrears and services included. Inspect the building's common areas and ask about maintenance history, management and any planned work.

Separate service charges from utilities, cooling and the cost of appointing a property manager. The [Dubai service-charge guide](/journal/dubai-apartment-service-charges-impact-on-rental-returns) shows how different charges affect income.

sections.heading: Which tenant and lease are you planning for?
sections.body:
For a long-term lease, compare recent signed rents for similar bedrooms, floor, condition, parking and furniture in the same building where possible. Record any rent-free period and how long the unit took to let. Compare asking rents with signed leases and the income collected from similar homes.

If considering a holiday home, verify the current permit, building rules and operator agreement with the relevant authority before making revenue assumptions. Budget for occupancy gaps, utilities, cleaning, platform and management costs. Short-term gross income is not directly comparable with a long-term rent without normalising expenses and time periods.

Test both the tenant's access and the unit's usability. A waterfront view or proximity to offices may be valuable to some occupants, but the premium depends on the property and actual evidence.

sections.heading: Assess future competition and exit
sections.body:
Review nearby projects and expected handovers alongside existing vacant or advertised units. A schedule may change, and a city-wide supply figure cannot establish what will happen in one building. Ask about the developer's progress and the local demand for the type of apartment you are considering.

Seek recent completed sales of comparable properties, noting the date, floor, condition and included parking. Separate asking prices from completed transactions. Include selling costs and any outstanding loan in a future cash calculation.

Compare projected yield with resale evidence, selling costs and your intended holding period. Make sure the investment remains manageable if the unit takes longer to let or sell.

sections.heading: Inspect how the investment will be managed
sections.body:
Ask who will arrange viewings, collect rent, manage the tenant relationship and coordinate repairs. If appointing a provider, check its licence and obtain a written agreement showing the fee basis, repair approval limits, reporting schedule and handling of funds. A building's common-area manager is not necessarily the manager of the individual tenancy.

Compare the time and cost involved if you manage the apartment yourself. Keep an allowance for maintenance inside the unit and ask how quickly essential repairs can be arranged when it is occupied. A convenient location cannot remove the need for a realistic operating plan. Revisit the calculation when a lease, service charge or management quote changes.

sections.heading: Compare current options
sections.body:
Browse [Aliyas Business Bay projects](/projects?emirate=Dubai&area=dubai-business-bay) and [Dubai Marina projects](/projects?emirate=Dubai&area=dubai-marina). Ask which specific units are currently available and request their plans, price, charges and terms. Compare each option using the same time period and assumptions.

[Contact Aliyas](/contact) with your budget and intended lease strategy. Verify the property, current costs and applicable permissions before committing.

aliyas-journal-147.excerpt: Compare Dubai Hills Estate and Dubai Creek Harbour for family living using the actual home, school run, daily travel, amenities and total cost.
aliyas-journal-147.introduction:
Dubai Hills Estate and Dubai Creek Harbour offer different family settings: one is organised around a large park and inland community facilities, while the other centres on a waterfront setting. The right choice depends on the specific building, school and work journeys, household budget and the spaces your family will use.

Compare actual homes and services that are open today. A community plan or proposed transport link is not the same as an operating service from your front door.
takeaways: Check the actual school and work routes, admissions and transport for each shortlisted home.
Inspect the apartment or villa, shared facilities and daily access rather than relying on community-wide descriptions.
Compare total housing, service-charge, transport and school costs using current written figures.

sections.heading: What is each community like?
sections.body:
[Emaar's Dubai Hills Estate guide](https://www.emaar.com/en/our-communities/dubai-hills-estate) describes a mixed community of apartments, villas and townhouses with Dubai Hills Park and Dubai Hills Mall. [Emaar's Dubai Creek Harbour community page](https://www.emaar.com/en/our-communities/dubai-creek-harbour) describes a waterfront setting with residential projects and public spaces. These developer descriptions are starting points; verify the facilities and access for your specific building.

At Dubai Hills, check the route from the home to the park, school and daily services you would use. At Creek Harbour, check the distance to the waterfront, building access and the services currently operating near your apartment. Visit on a working day and in the evening.

A promised view or amenity should be checked against the unit's plan and contract, not inferred from a general community image.

rows: Check access to the park and local services
Check access to the waterfront and local services
Test the actual journeys and admissions
Test the same journeys and admissions
Inspect layout, parking and building facilities
Inspect layout, parking and building facilities
Request full housing and running costs
Use the same cost and time period

sections.heading: Test school, work and transport
sections.body:
List the schools and workplaces your family actually uses. Ask each school about admission, fees, transport and the applicable year group. A nearby school is not an assured place or bus service from every building. Test the route at school and work times, including the return.

The RTA describes the approved [Dubai Metro Blue Line project](https://www.rta.ae/wps/portal/rta/ae/public-transport/metro/about-metro?lang=en), including a planned Dubai Creek Harbour station. It is a project, not evidence of a service already operating at the apartment. Check the latest official status and current transport options when deciding.

Consider how household members without a car will reach their regular destinations. Parking, a second car or school transport can change the total cost of a location.

sections.heading: Inspect the home for your family's routine
sections.body:
Check bedrooms, storage, kitchen, laundry, balcony access and the position of bathrooms. Measure spaces for existing furniture and consider step-free access or stairs for children and older relatives. An advertised bedroom count does not show whether a layout works for your family.

Inspect cooling, plumbing, windows and visible moisture. Check the allocated parking space, lift access, common areas and the rules and condition of a pool or play area if those facilities matter. If an apartment is off-plan, review the signed plan, specification and handover provisions rather than assuming the display home is identical.

Arrange a suitable professional inspection where needed and record agreed repairs or included items in writing. A family viewing at different times can reveal noise or access issues missed on the first visit.

sections.heading: Compare the full household cost
sections.body:
For a purchase, add the price, buyer-paid transaction and financing charges, service charges, insurance and repairs. For a rental, include annual rent, payment dates, deposits and fees, utilities and the lease's maintenance terms. Add school transport and commuting where they differ between homes. Request written quotes and keep refundable deposits separate from non-refundable expenses.

The chart shows one family's sample weighting for selecting a home: layout and condition 35 points, daily travel 30, affordability 25 and amenities 10. It is not a score for either community or a claim that one is better. Change the weights and set non-negotiables for your own family.

The [Dubai buying cost guide](/journal/total-upfront-cost-of-buying-property-in-dubai) explains purchase cost categories, while the [JVC and Arjan guide](/journal/jvc-vs-arjan-apartment-investment-comparison) offers another example of building-level checks.

chart.title: Example family decision weights
chart.note: Sample weights total 100 points and do not rate either community.

sections.heading: Check ownership and future plans
sections.body:
For a purchase, confirm the buyer's right, title or initial registration, seller authority and any mortgage or tenancy for the exact unit. Ask for the current service-charge statement and developer clearance. If a project is under construction, verify its status, payment recipient and contract through the relevant official channels.

For a rental, review the lease, deposit, maintenance responsibilities, renewal and early-exit terms. Ask what happens if a promised facility is unavailable. Obtain a written agreement rather than relying on a verbal assurance.

Consider how the home will fit if the family grows or a school or workplace changes. A community that looks convenient on a map should still pass the household's actual routine and budget tests.

sections.heading: Visit the spaces your family will use
sections.body:
Walk the route from the building entrance to the park, waterfront or nearby shops with the family members who will use it. Check crossings, lift access and the practical distance with a pushchair or other equipment. Ask whether a shared facility is included in the building's charge or requires a separate payment.

A community may have attractive amenities, but their value depends on whether they are open, accessible and suitable for your household. Record the opening times and any restrictions, and compare them with your normal working and school week.

sections.heading: Explore current homes
sections.body:
Browse [Aliyas Dubai Hills Estate projects](/projects?emirate=Dubai&area=dubai-hills-estate) and [Dubai Creek Harbour projects](/projects?emirate=Dubai&area=dubai-creek-harbour). Ask which exact homes are currently available and request their plans, current prices and terms.

[Contact Aliyas](/contact) with your family size, school and work destinations and complete budget. Visit the home and confirm the documents and costs before making a decision.

aliyas-journal-148.excerpt: Compare renting in Jumeirah Lakes Towers and Dubai Marina using the actual apartment, daily routes, lease terms and total annual cost.
aliyas-journal-148.introduction:
Jumeirah Lakes Towers (JLT) and Dubai Marina offer different everyday settings, but the right rental depends on the specific tower, your route to work and the terms of the lease. Compare homes with similar size and condition, then add transport, utilities and move-in cash to the advertised rent.

The worked example below shows how household costs can be compared. The example provides a consistent way to compare the costs of two rental homes.
takeaways: Visit the actual building and test the route to the station, workplace and regular services.
Compare annual rent together with transport, utilities and non-refundable lease costs.
Check deposits, maintenance, renewal and early-exit clauses before paying.

sections.heading: How do the neighbourhoods differ?
sections.body:
[DMCC describes JLT](https://dmcc.ae/destination) as a mixed residential and commercial district with lakes, parkland, retail and dining. [Emaar's Dubai Marina guide](https://www.emaar.com/en/our-communities/dubai-marina) describes a waterfront setting with a promenade and residential towers. These broad descriptions are a starting point; individual buildings differ in access, condition and facilities.

The [RTA metro and tram station map](https://www.rta.ae/wps/portal/rta/ae/public-transport/metro-stations-map) lists stations in the wider JLT and Marina corridor. Check the current service and the real walking route from the tower, including crossings and the final journey to your destination. A station serving an area does not mean every building is a short walk away.

Visit at the times you will travel and compare noise, parking, lift access and nearby services. For wider Dubai housing context, see the [family community comparison](/journal/dubai-hills-estate-vs-dubai-creek-harbour-for-families).

sections.heading: Compare the whole annual cost
sections.body:
Imagine a JLT apartment with AED 100,000 annual rent and AED 8,000 transport cost, and a Marina apartment with AED 110,000 rent and AED 3,000 transport cost. The combined amounts are AED 108,000 and AED 113,000. These examples show how rent and transport costs can be compared for two different homes.

The chart compares only those two categories. Add utilities, cooling, internet, parking, agency and lease charges, as well as any differences in size or included furnishings. A lower combined figure may not be the better choice if the home or commute does not meet your needs.

List refundable deposits separately: they affect the cash needed to move even if returned in full later. Confirm the actual payment dates and written terms for each apartment.

chart.title: Example annual rent plus transport
chart.note: Sample inputs; excludes utilities, deposits, fees and other household costs.

sections.heading: Inspect the apartment and building
sections.body:
Check the layout, storage, windows, cooling, water pressure and visible condition. Ask about noise from roads, construction or shared areas, and visit at a second time if possible. Confirm which appliances and furniture are included and whether parking is allocated to the unit.

Walk from the parking space or entrance to the lift and apartment. Check the operating condition and rules of any pool or gym that matters to you. Ask building management how to report faults and whether move-in permits or deposits are required.

Record pre-existing issues and agree an inventory at handover. A photograph of the project is not evidence that the actual apartment has the same view or finish.

sections.heading: Read the lease and register it
sections.body:
Request the annual rent, instalment dates, deposit amount, brokerage and other fees, and whether utilities and cooling are included. Read the clauses on repairs, renewal, notice and early termination. Ask for written clarification before signing if an obligation is unclear.

DLD's [register or renew tenancy contract service](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/register-renew-ejari-contract/) describes Ejari registration, available channels and current service fees. Confirm the relevant process and who pays for your agreement. Verify that the landlord or representative has authority to lease the unit.

Keep receipts, the registered contract, an inventory and a dated condition record. Ask how and when the security deposit will be assessed at the end of the tenancy.

sections.heading: Choose for your routine, not the label
sections.body:
List your non-negotiables: budget, bedroom layout, acceptable door-to-door travel and the facilities you will actually use. A home close to a preferred promenade may involve a longer school or work journey; a tower near a station may still require a crossing or a long lift wait. Check the specific route.

If two options are close in cost, compare the quality of the lease, management responsiveness and condition of the apartment. Consider the ability to move if your circumstances change, and include any early-exit cost specified in the agreement.

Do not assume a particular building has the same management, cooling arrangement or parking terms as another tower in the same community.

sections.heading: Plan the cash needed to move
sections.body:
Ask for a dated breakdown of the first rent instalment, security deposit, agency charge, Ejari registration, utility deposits and moving costs. Some items may be refundable, but the cash is still needed at the start. Confirm whether a move-in permit, lift booking or building deposit applies to the particular tower.

Put later rent cheques and any annual payments on a calendar alongside income. If an apartment is furnished, agree a list of items and their condition; if it is unfurnished, include the cost of furniture you need. Request evidence that existing utility balances are settled and ask when services can be connected.

sections.heading: Ask about current rental options
sections.body:
Browse the [Aliyas Dubai Marina projects](/projects?emirate=Dubai&area=dubai-marina) for local context and ask which relevant rental homes in JLT or Marina are currently available. A project page is not itself a rental offer.

[Contact Aliyas](/contact) with your budget, required bedrooms and travel destinations. Request the exact address, written lease terms and a viewing of the actual apartment.

aliyas-journal-149.excerpt: Shortlist family communities for a DIFC commute by comparing the actual home, school route, transport and full household budget.
aliyas-journal-149.introduction:
The best Dubai community for a family working in DIFC depends on the exact office entrance, school, working hours and housing needs. A central apartment may reduce one journey, while a home farther away may offer a different layout or outdoor setting. Test the complete family routine before choosing.

Use DIFC and nearby Business Bay, Dubai Hills Estate and Dubai Creek Harbour as starting points. The right building and current transport options matter more than a single advertised drive time.
takeaways: Measure the door-to-door work and school journeys from each actual building.
Compare the home, open facilities and total household cost, not just distance to DIFC.
Treat planned transport links as future projects until the current official service is confirmed.

sections.heading: Which communities should you shortlist?
sections.body:
DIFC is a mixed business and residential district; check the specific building's layout, school journey and access to the office. [Bayut's Business Bay guide](https://www.bayut.com/area-guides/business-bay/) describes a nearby mixed-use area around the Dubai Water Canal. A particular Business Bay tower can have a different route and street environment from another part of the district.

[Dubai Hills Estate](https://www.emaar.com/en/our-communities/dubai-hills-estate) offers a park-centred setting described by its developer, while [Dubai Creek Harbour](https://www.emaar.com/en/our-communities/dubai-creek-harbour) is a waterfront community. The [Dubai Hills and Creek Harbour family guide](/journal/dubai-hills-estate-vs-dubai-creek-harbour-for-families) compares their practical family considerations.

Use these communities as a starting point for your search and compare homes that meet your needs. Visit the exact street and home before deciding.

rows: Building, school route and total housing cost
Actual office route and tower access
School and work journeys from the home

sections.heading: Test the commute and school run together
sections.body:
Record the time from the apartment door to the DIFC office on a normal working day, including parking, walking and any transport transfer. Repeat the return trip. If a parent drops children at school, test that combined route rather than a direct home-to-office journey that the family will not actually take.

The [RTA metro and tram map](https://www.rta.ae/wps/portal/rta/ae/public-transport/metro-stations-map) lists Financial Centre, Emirates Towers and Business Bay stations. Check the current service and walking route to your building and office entrance; station names do not establish a particular journey time.

Ask schools about places, curriculum, fees and bus service for the exact address. Ask schools about admission, transport and collection times for your address.

sections.heading: Inspect the home and family facilities
sections.body:
Check bedroom layout, storage, kitchen, laundry, lift access and parking. If you have young children, inspect balcony and window access and the route to any play area. Ask whether the facility is currently operating, included in the rent or charge and subject to restrictions.

For a ready home, inspect cooling, plumbing, noise and visible condition. For off-plan, check the signed specification, payment schedule and handover terms. Compare the finished apartment with the signed plan and specifications.

Visit at a second time to observe traffic and noise. Check whether household members without a car can reach the services they need while the commuter is at work.

sections.heading: Compare the full family budget
sections.body:
For a rental, add rent, payment dates, non-refundable fees, utilities and any transport or parking cost. For a purchase, include transaction and financing costs, service charges, maintenance and insurance. Add school transport and any second car if the location requires them. Request current written figures for the actual home.

The chart shows a sample household weighting: layout and condition 30 points, work travel 30, school routine 25 and affordability 15. It is a way to organise a decision, not a score or price ranking for the listed communities. Change the priorities to suit your family.

Keep a separate reserve and account for large payments that fall on different dates. A monthly average can conceal a rent cheque or school instalment due at the start of a term.

chart.title: Example family decision priorities
chart.note: Sample weights total 100 points; they do not rate the communities.

sections.heading: Check the documents and future changes
sections.body:
For a purchase, verify the buyer's right, title or initial registration, seller authority, mortgage or tenancy, and the unit's current building charges. For a rental, review the lease, deposit, maintenance, renewal and early-exit clauses. Ask for the official registration process and written quote for the transaction.

If a new transport link or school is part of the decision, verify its current status with the provider and make sure the family can manage if the planned opening changes. Do not budget as if a proposed service is already operating.

Consider whether the home would remain suitable if your office attendance, school or family size changes. A short commute for one person is not the only measure of a workable home.

sections.heading: Compare the week, not one journey
sections.body:
Create a simple weekly timetable for each shortlisted home. Mark office days, school drop-offs, activities and the trips made by other household members. A home that saves one adult fifteen minutes on a single journey may add several separate trips elsewhere; the relevant comparison is the routine your family will actually follow.

Check alternatives for days when a car is unavailable or a train is disrupted. If working hours are flexible, test whether a different departure time changes the route. Keep the observations with the cost worksheet so the final choice reflects both time and money, without assuming that one published travel estimate applies to every household.

sections.body:
Browse [Aliyas Business Bay projects](/projects?emirate=Dubai&area=dubai-business-bay), [Dubai Hills Estate projects](/projects?emirate=Dubai&area=dubai-hills-estate) and [Dubai Creek Harbour projects](/projects?emirate=Dubai&area=dubai-creek-harbour). Ask which homes are currently available for your intended use.

[Contact Aliyas](/contact) with your budget, preferred bedrooms, school and office destinations. Request the exact address, plan and terms, then test the actual journeys before committing.

aliyas-journal-150.excerpt: Compare short-term and long-term Dubai rental income after occupancy, operating costs, permits and management rather than headline revenue.
aliyas-journal-150.introduction:
A Dubai holiday home can generate a different pattern of revenue and expenses from an annual tenancy. A higher nightly gross amount does not necessarily mean more money for the owner after empty nights, cleaning, utilities, management and building charges. Compare both strategies over the same period using evidence for the actual apartment.

Holiday-home operation also requires the applicable Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism (DET) registration and permit. The worked example below compares the costs of the two rental strategies over the same period.
takeaways: Compare net income over the same year, including vacancy or occupancy and all owner-paid costs.
Check DET registration, the unit permit and building rules before operating a holiday home.
Test seasonality, operator fees and repairs; neither strategy guarantees a return.

sections.heading: Start with permitted use and the unit
sections.body:
DET's [holiday-home permit service](https://www.dubaidet.gov.ae/en/our-services/for-consumers-and-students/issue-a-new-holiday-homes-permit) describes applying for a residential unit to operate as a holiday home. Its [operator registration service](https://www.dubaidet.gov.ae/our-services/for-consumers-and-students/register-as-a-holiday-home-operator) explains registration through the Holiday Homes system. Confirm current eligibility, documents, fees, guest requirements and any operator licence with DET before listing or operating.

Check the building's rules and your mortgage, insurance and management agreement for the intended use. A residential unit and a long-term lease do not automatically establish that a holiday-home permit has been issued.

The [Business Bay and Dubai Marina investment guide](/journal/business-bay-vs-dubai-marina-rental-investment) provides area context, but the unit's permit and actual operating costs still need verification.

table.caption: Compare the two strategies consistently
rows: Occupied nights multiplied by realised nightly income
Rent actually collected over the same year
Seasonal empty nights and booking gaps
Void periods and any rent-free period
Cleaning, utilities, platform, permits and operator
Service charge, repairs and landlord management
DET registration, unit permit and building rules
Tenant turnover, renewal and payment risk

sections.heading: Calculate a sample year
sections.body:
Suppose a holiday home earns an average AED 650 per occupied night for 219 nights, equal to AED 142,350 of gross income. Assume cleaning AED 18,000, utilities AED 12,000, management AED 28,470, permit-related costs AED 3,500, building charges AED 16,000 and maintenance AED 8,000. These sample expenses total AED 85,970, leaving AED 56,380 before finance, tax and sale costs.

For the long-term alternative, assume AED 100,000 rent, AED 5,000 vacancy allowance and AED 27,500 of owner expenses, leaving AED 67,500 before finance, tax and sale costs. The chart shows the two results. All inputs are examples; actual occupancy, rates, fees and obligations vary.

This example excludes financing, initial furniture, replacement reserves and any pass-through guest levies. Add the items relevant to your own agreement and avoid counting a guest-paid levy as owner revenue.

chart.title: Example annual net operating income
chart.note: Sample assumptions; the comparison excludes financing, tax, initial furnishing and sale costs.

sections.heading: Build realistic short-term assumptions
sections.body:
Use comparable permitted properties with similar location, bedrooms, condition and amenities. Check whether displayed nightly prices are before platform charges, discounts or cleaning fees. Estimate occupied nights by season and allow for blocked dates, maintenance and gaps between bookings. A full calendar at the advertised rate is rarely a sound starting assumption.

Ask an operator for a written schedule of management and platform fees, cleaning, linen, utilities, maintenance, insurance and permit costs. Clarify whether percentages are charged on gross booking value or a different base and whether applicable tax is included.

Review the DET process for guest registration and reporting, and establish who is responsible. Confirm the permitted use and current requirements, and compare an operator’s revenue estimate with documented costs.

sections.heading: Build the long-term alternative
sections.body:
Use recent signed leases for similar units and record the lease term, furnishing, parking, included services and any rent-free period. Deduct a vacancy allowance, service charges, management, maintenance and insurance paid by the owner. The [Dubai net yield guide](/journal/how-to-calculate-net-rental-yield-in-dubai) explains how to compare the resulting income with total acquisition cost.

DLD's [tenancy registration service](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/register-renew-ejari-contract/) describes registering or renewing a contract through Ejari. Confirm the current charges and each party's responsibilities under the actual agreement.

Include the cost of switching strategies, such as furnishing or removing furniture, and any downtime between tenancies. A long-term lease also has contractual notice and renewal terms.

sections.heading: Test a downside and the work involved
sections.body:
Recalculate the holiday-home case with fewer occupied nights, a lower realised rate and an urgent repair. Recalculate the long-term case with a longer void or non-payment and an additional repair. If a strategy only works under a full-occupancy assumption, review the investment and reserve.

Consider who responds to guests or tenants, arranges cleaning and repairs, maintains records and renews permits. A higher projected net income may require substantially more management time. Ask a licensed operator about service standards, reporting, repair authority and termination before signing.

Neither operating income figure includes the outstanding mortgage, personal tax position or eventual sale price. Prepare those separately for a full investment decision.

sections.heading: Estimate the occupancy needed to match the alternative
sections.body:
In the sample holiday-home example, suppose the AED 650 nightly income and 20% management charge remain unchanged, leaving AED 520 per occupied night before the other listed costs. If those other costs were fixed at AED 57,500, matching the long-term example's AED 67,500 would require about 241 occupied nights, or roughly 66% of a 365-day year. This break-even calculation shows how rental income and expenses interact.

In practice cleaning, utilities and other expenses can rise with occupancy, while rates can change by season and booking channel. Recalculate using your operator's actual fee basis and variable costs, and include any additional obligations. A break-even point based on unrealistic fixed costs will give false confidence.

sections.heading: Review a specific property
sections.body:
Browse the [Aliyas Dubai project collection](/projects?emirate=Dubai) and [contact Aliyas](/contact) with your property, budget and intended strategy. Ask for the building's current charges and the documents needed to assess permitted use.

Verify the holiday-home permit requirements with DET or the tenancy process with DLD, and use unit-specific evidence rather than the worked example.

aliyas-journal-151.excerpt: Compare furnished and unfurnished Dubai rental investments using collected rent, furnishing costs, tenant fit and ongoing owner expenses.
aliyas-journal-151.introduction:
Furnishing a Dubai rental can change the tenants a home attracts and the rent it may achieve, but the extra revenue must be weighed against furniture, replacement, management and vacancy costs. Compare the actual apartment over your intended holding period rather than assuming furnished always earns a better return.

This guide focuses on an owner's long-term rental decision. The calculation uses example figures to show how furnishing and operating costs affect rental income.
takeaways: Compare collected rent after vacancy and owner costs, including furniture purchase and replacement.
Use an agreed inventory and clear repair, damage and deposit terms for supplied items.
Check whether the intended lease is long-term or a permitted holiday home; their obligations differ.

sections.heading: What changes when the owner furnishes?
sections.body:
A furnished offer may include beds, seating, dining furniture, appliances, curtains and kitchen equipment, but the actual list must be agreed. A partly furnished home can have a different cost and tenant appeal. Prepare an inventory with the condition of each item and clarify who maintains or replaces it.

Compare recent signed leases for similar apartments in the same building with the same parking, condition and included services. Record whether each is furnished and what that means in the lease. Compare advertised rents with signed leases and the time taken to let similar homes.

The [Business Bay and Dubai Marina area guide](/journal/business-bay-vs-dubai-marina-rental-investment) provides location context, while the exact building and tenant determine the relevant comparison.

table.caption: Owner's furnished versus unfurnished worksheet
rows: Any appliances or work still required

sections.heading: Compare first-year cash
sections.body:
Assume a sample furnished option collects AED 96,000 after vacancy, has AED 20,000 owner operating costs and requires AED 12,000 of furniture in the first year. The remaining cash before finance and tax is AED 64,000. A sample unfurnished option collects AED 87,000 after vacancy and has AED 18,000 of owner costs, leaving AED 69,000.

The furnished unit collects more rent but produces less first-year cash in this example because of setup costs. The chart shows those sample results. The example compares how furnishing and operating costs affect the two rental strategies.

For later years, do not charge the full initial furniture purchase again, but budget for wear, replacement, storage and the value recovered when the furniture is sold. A cash-flow calculation and accounting depreciation are different measures.

chart.title: Example first-year cash before finance and tax
chart.note: Sample inputs; the furnished example includes AED 12,000 of first-year furniture spending.

sections.heading: Evaluate the full holding period
sections.body:
Estimate furniture purchase, delivery, installation, replacement and removal over the years you expect to own the apartment. Compare the additional collected rent after vacancy with those costs. If the home will be sold furnished, be conservative about the value a buyer will pay for used items.

Run a shorter holding-period scenario. A large initial outlay may be harder to recover if the tenant leaves early or you sell sooner than planned. Also test a lower rent premium and a major appliance replacement.

Include the unit's building service charges, management, repairs and insurance in both cases. DLD's [service charge index](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/service-charge-index/) helps check approved community charges; request the statement and area basis for the exact unit.

sections.heading: Agree the lease and inventory
sections.body:
List every included item, its condition and any serial number where useful. Take dated photographs with the tenant and agree how faults should be reported, who will arrange repairs and how damage and normal wear will be assessed. Confirm the deposit and return process in the written lease.

DLD's [tenancy registration service](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/register-renew-ejari-contract/) describes registering or renewing a contract through Ejari. Check the current process and fees, and verify the landlord's or representative's authority.

If you appoint a manager, agree the fee basis, inspection schedule, repair approval limits and reporting. Avoid assuming an annual management quote includes furniture replacement or a new tenant placement fee.

sections.heading: Distinguish long-term and holiday-home use
sections.body:
A furnished long-term lease is not automatically a holiday-home operation. If considering short stays, verify DET registration, the unit permit and current building rules before operating. Cleaning, utilities, guest support and seasonal occupancy can produce a very different cost structure.

The [short-term versus long-term rental guide](/journal/how-to-compare-short-term-and-long-term-rental-income-in-dubai) explains how to compare those strategies on the same annual basis. Do not compare a nightly gross rate directly with annual net rent.

For either strategy, check insurance, lender restrictions and the agreement with any operator. Compare the advertised rent with furnishing, service charges and maintenance to assess net income.

sections.heading: Estimate the rent premium needed
sections.body:
As a simple starting point, divide the expected net cost of furniture by the years you intend to use it. If a sample AED 12,000 setup has no resale value and lasts three years, the cost is AED 4,000 per year before replacement, financing and the timing of payments. The furnished home would need at least that much additional annual net income to cover this narrow cost.

Add delivery, repairs, replacement and any extra vacancy or management charge before drawing a conclusion. If you expect resale proceeds, test a case where they are lower or zero. Keep the actual upfront cash requirement separate from the annual comparison.

sections.heading: Assess a current property
sections.body:
Browse the [Aliyas Dubai project collection](/projects?emirate=Dubai) and [contact Aliyas](/contact) with the apartment, budget and intended lease. Ask for current building charges and comparable lease evidence, then calculate both options using the specific unit's terms. Record the dates and sources of those figures so the comparison can be updated when the lease or costs change.

Keep a reserve for vacancy and repairs and verify the applicable official requirements before letting.

aliyas-journal-152.excerpt: Plan a Dubai sale of mortgaged property using a current bank liability letter, DLD registration, mortgage release and a clear settlement schedule.
aliyas-journal-152.introduction:
A mortgaged Dubai property can be sold through a process that coordinates the lender, buyer, seller and Dubai Land Department (DLD). The outstanding debt and registered mortgage must be addressed as part of the transaction. Start with a current liability letter and agree the settlement and release sequence before promising a completion date.

The exact documents, charges and timing depend on the property and parties. Verify them with the bank, DLD and the relevant developer or trustee for your transaction.
takeaways: Request a dated bank liability or settlement letter and check any early-settlement charges.
DLD describes registering a mortgaged property for sale, then completing the sale after the bank's release letter is submitted.
Agree how debt, sale proceeds, fees and any new buyer mortgage will be handled in writing.

sections.heading: 1. Confirm the debt and the property documents
sections.body:
Ask the lender for a current liability or settlement statement, its validity period, early-settlement terms and the steps needed for a mortgage release. A balance shown on an old statement may differ from the amount required on completion. Check whether other loans or registered interests affect the property.

Gather the title, seller identification, any power of attorney, current service-charge statement and developer clearance requirements. If the property is tenanted, review the lease, deposit and possession terms before promising a vacant handover. Verify the buyer's right to acquire the property.

DLD's [mortgaged property sale service](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/registering-the-sale-of-a-mortgaged-property/) lists a bank liability letter and identification among the required documents. Confirm the current list and process for your transaction.

table.caption: Documents and decisions for a mortgaged sale
rows: Establish the amount, validity and release process
Confirm the property and authorised parties
Record price, dates, payment allocation and conditions
Complete the registered release and sale steps

sections.heading: 2. Agree the sale and settlement sequence
sections.body:
DLD describes a trustee-centre process in which a mortgaged property is registered for sale, the bank indebtedness is addressed and a mortgage release letter is submitted before completion of the sale and any new mortgage procedure. The service page lists manager's cheques allocated to the bank or developer, seller and department for its stated process. Confirm current payment instructions directly with the trustee and lender.

Record the price, deposit, allocation of fees, target dates and what happens if the bank release or buyer financing is delayed. If the buyer also needs a mortgage, coordinate the two lenders and confirm whether the procedures can be completed together. Do not assume every sale follows the same timing.

Use traceable payment arrangements and verify the recipient independently. A deposit or initial reservation is not a completed transfer.

sections.heading: 3. Estimate the cash remaining
sections.body:
Imagine a sale for AED 2,000,000, with an AED 1,100,000 loan settlement, AED 10,000 in assumed bank settlement costs, AED 40,000 selling commission and AED 5,000 in assumed clearance costs. The remaining cash is AED 845,000 before other transaction charges, tax and any adjustments. These example inputs show how the settlement and transfer amounts fit into the overall calculation.

The chart shows the allocation of the sample sale price. This is not profit: calculating profit also requires the original acquisition cost, holding costs and other relevant cash flows. Confirm which fees the seller actually pays under the agreement.

If the debt and costs exceed the sale price, discuss the shortfall and bank requirements before agreeing to a sale. Do not assume the lender will release the mortgage without the required settlement.

chart.title: Example allocation of mortgaged sale proceeds
chart.note: Sample amounts allocate AED 2,000,000 and exclude other charges and the original purchase cost.

sections.heading: 4. Check the release and transfer fees
sections.body:
DLD's [mortgage release service](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/request-for-mortgage-termination) lists the release process and charges for different channels. Its mortgaged-sale page lists additional procedure and service partner fees. The applicable combination can depend on the transaction and timing, so request one itemised current quote rather than adding figures from several pages without checking for overlap.

Ask the bank about its own early-settlement and administrative charges, and agree which party pays each item. The sale registration amount and a new buyer mortgage, if any, are separate from the seller's outstanding loan.

Retain the bank release letter, receipts and DLD confirmation. Confirm the registered outcome before treating the sale as complete or handing over possession under the agreement.

sections.heading: 5. Plan for tenants and handover
sections.body:
If the apartment is rented, provide the buyer with accurate lease and deposit information and agree how rent paid beyond transfer will be handled. Seek advice about the tenant's rights and notice obligations. A sale does not make a tenant disappear automatically.

After the agreed completion, record keys, access cards, parking and meter readings. Reconcile the sale price, debt settlement and charges with the trustee and lender, and keep copies of the final documents.

For market context, the [Business Bay and Marina area guide](/journal/business-bay-vs-dubai-marina-rental-investment) explains why comparable evidence and building charges matter to a buyer. The process above applies only to the relevant property's current circumstances.

sections.heading: Agree what happens if timing changes
sections.body:
A liability letter can expire, a bank may need more documents or a buyer's financing may take longer than expected. Ask the lender and trustee how to refresh the settlement amount and what notice is needed if the proposed completion date changes. Record the agreed conditions and consequences in the sale documents.

If the buyer pays an amount intended to settle the seller's debt, obtain suitable advice about how the transaction is protected and documented. Confirm payment details directly with the bank or approved transaction channel before transferring funds. Each party should understand when the mortgage release, ownership transfer and possession occur and who holds the evidence.

sections.heading: Discuss the property and current process
sections.body:
Browse the [Aliyas Dubai project collection](/projects?emirate=Dubai) and [contact Aliyas](/contact) with the unit, lender and intended sale timing. Request a current market discussion and written service terms.

Confirm the settlement amount, release procedure and official fees with the bank and DLD before signing or arranging payments.

references.period: Official service and process; checked 8 November 2026

references.period: Official release service; checked 8 November 2026

aliyas-journal-153.excerpt: Check a Dubai off-plan resale by verifying the seller's registered interest, amounts paid, remaining instalments, project status and transfer conditions.
aliyas-journal-153.introduction:
Buying an off-plan resale means acquiring an existing buyer's interest before the development is complete. The buyer needs to understand both the amount payable to the seller and the instalments still owed under the developer's contract. Verify the registered interest and transfer requirements before treating the quoted premium as the total price.

The arithmetic below is an example. The actual transfer process, fees and payment allocation depend on the contract, developer and Dubai Land Department (DLD) requirements.
takeaways: Verify the seller's initial registration, authority, original contract and current payment statement.
Add the amount payable to the seller, remaining developer instalments and transaction costs.
Confirm project status, developer clearance, any mortgage and the buyer's registered outcome.

sections.heading: 1. Verify the seller and the project
sections.body:
Request the initial registration document, original sale agreement, unit plan, seller identity and evidence of authority to sell. Match the unit number, project and buyer details across the documents. Ask the developer for a current account statement showing amounts paid, upcoming instalments and any overdue balance.

Use DLD's [project status enquiry](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/real-estate-project-status-landing/real-estate-project-status/) to check the exact project, developer and available escrow information. Confirm the status and any discrepancy with the department and developer. A project completion percentage is a dated measure, not a guarantee of a handover date.

The [Dubai off-plan verification guide](/journal/how-to-check-a-dubai-off-plan-project-before-buying) provides additional checks for the project and payment recipient. Do not rely solely on an advertisement or the seller's verbal description.

table.caption: Off-plan resale due diligence
rows: Initial registration, identity and authority to transfer
Original price, receipts, arrears and remaining instalments
DLD status, developer, construction and escrow details
Developer conditions, clearance, fees and DLD procedure
New registration, future obligations and payment records

sections.heading: 2. Calculate the complete purchase commitment
sections.body:
Imagine an original contract price of AED 1,000,000, with AED 400,000 already paid and AED 600,000 still due to the developer. If the parties agree a resale price of AED 1,100,000 and the buyer pays the seller AED 500,000 while assuming the AED 600,000 balance, the combined price is AED 1,100,000 before fees. The AED 500,000 includes the seller's paid amount and a sample AED 100,000 premium.

The chart separates the seller payment and remaining instalments. These amounts and the allocation are examples; actual arrangements may differ and must be documented and verified. Add DLD, developer, brokerage, finance and other agreed charges to find total capital required.

Check whether any overdue instalment, penalty, incentive or discount changes the calculation. Do not count a paid instalment twice or assume the seller's asking premium is the whole buyer commitment.

chart.title: Example resale price components
chart.note: Sample components total AED 1,100,000 before fees; actual payment allocation requires written confirmation.

sections.heading: 3. Confirm transfer conditions and charges
sections.body:
Ask the developer and DLD whether the unit can currently be transferred, what clearance or consent is required and how the new buyer's interest will be registered. Check the original contract's resale terms and the current account status. Do not assume a standard minimum payment percentage applies to every project.

DLD's [real estate legislation compilation](https://dubailand.gov.ae/media/x0bf21ii/book.pdf) includes provisions on the interim property register and approved administrative expenses. Confirm the current applicable law and obtain a written itemised fee quote for the transaction.

If the seller's interest is mortgaged or pledged, ask the lender and parties how release or transfer will be handled. Agree the sequence and conditions in writing, including what happens if clearance or registration cannot be completed.

sections.heading: 4. Review the obligations you will take over
sections.body:
Read the full sale agreement, payment dates, specification, handover provisions, delay and default clauses, and any amendment or incentive. Confirm whether the buyer inherits remaining obligations and how the developer will acknowledge them. Ask a qualified adviser to explain terms or documents you do not understand.

Map instalments and other costs on a calendar. Keep a reserve if construction or finance is delayed, and do not depend on a future resale or rental income to pay a contractual instalment. The [post-handover plan guide](/journal/how-to-compare-post-handover-payment-plans-in-dubai) explains how to test later payments.

Verify payment instructions directly through independently confirmed channels. A receipt should identify the relevant payer, unit and transaction.

sections.heading: 5. Check the registered outcome and eventual handover
sections.body:
Confirm which party submits the transfer and how the buyer receives updated initial registration. Check the buyer name, unit and remaining obligations on the issued documents. Keep the original contract, transfer agreement, receipts and developer statement together.

Ask for dated construction updates and the process for inspection and handover. A premium paid today does not guarantee a higher value later. Compare current alternatives and recent evidence, and allow for competing supply, a delayed handover or a lower eventual rent.

The [JVC and Arjan area guide](/journal/jvc-vs-arjan-apartment-investment-comparison) illustrates why a location and building need their own assessment; use the specific project's records for the final decision.

sections.heading: Compare the resale with a new unit
sections.body:
A resale price may differ from a developer's current offer because of the unit's floor, layout, view, payment schedule or timing. Compare the complete price and remaining obligations for genuinely similar alternatives, not just the premium requested by the existing buyer. Check whether incentives in the original contract transfer to the new buyer and whether any condition must be met.

Ask for current project information and a written statement of all charges. If a seller has paid more or less than expected, reconcile that amount with the developer before calculating the buyer's payment. An attractive premium can conceal a large remaining balance or an imminent instalment.

sections.heading: Discuss a specific resale
sections.body:
Browse the [Aliyas Dubai project collection](/projects?emirate=Dubai) and [contact Aliyas](/contact) with the project, unit and budget. Ask for the current seller statement, remaining schedule and written transfer conditions.

Verify the registered interest, official charges and payment recipient before signing or transferring funds.
