aliyas-journal-154.excerpt: Use recent Dubai transaction records to set an apartment resale price, adjust for unit differences and recognise limitations in the data.
aliyas-journal-154.introduction:
A defensible Dubai apartment resale price starts with recent completed transactions for genuinely comparable homes. Filter the evidence by area, building, property type and date, then assess differences in size, floor, condition, parking and tenancy. An asking price or an emirate-wide average is useful context but is not a completed sale of your apartment.

This guide explains the method using worked examples. It does not provide a formal valuation or claim that the sample transactions occurred.
takeaways: Use DLD transaction data and verify the type, date and property details before selecting comparables.
Adjust for meaningful differences and use a range when the available evidence is limited.
Separate the estimated market price from the seller's net proceeds after mortgage and selling costs.

sections.heading: Where can you find transaction evidence?
sections.body:
DLD's [real estate data page](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/open-data/real-estate-data/) offers filters including date, transaction type, registration type, area and property type. Its displayed fields include transaction amount, size, rooms, parking and project information. Check the definitions and coverage before using a record as a comparable sale.

Select completed sales rather than mixing mortgages, gifts, valuations or initial registrations into the same price comparison. Check the date and whether the record represents a similar completed apartment. Where a field is unavailable or the transaction terms are unclear, record the limitation rather than assuming a match.

The [Business Bay and Marina area guide](/journal/business-bay-vs-dubai-marina-rental-investment) explains why local building and tenant characteristics also matter.

table.caption: Comparable transaction worksheet
rows: Confirm a relevant completed sale and the period
Find genuinely similar apartments and measurement basis
Identify differences that may affect price
Check what the buyer receives and when
Record the reason, evidence and uncertainty

sections.heading: Choose and adjust the comparables
sections.body:
Start with the same building where enough recent evidence exists, then consider similar nearby buildings if necessary. A renovated apartment, different floor, view or parking arrangement may justify an adjustment. The size and direction of an adjustment should be supported by evidence, not an assumed percentage applied to every unit.

Price per square foot can help compare similar apartments, but only if the area measure is consistent. Check whether the recorded size includes balconies or other areas. A per-unit comparison can be more useful when the homes are close in size and layout.

Separate new off-plan sales from completed resales and check whether incentives or unusual payment terms affect the recorded value. If the data cannot establish those details, widen the range and seek more evidence.

sections.heading: Sample median, not an appraisal
sections.body:
Suppose three sample comparable sales are AED 1,600,000, AED 1,700,000 and AED 1,800,000. The median is AED 1,700,000. If the subject needs AED 30,000 of evidenced repairs and no other differences are assumed, a simplified starting point might be AED 1,670,000. The market effect of repairs may differ from their quoted cost.

The chart shows only the sample sale prices. Use the calculation to organise comparable sales before assessing a particular apartment. A professional would assess the relevance of each comparable and other differences before reaching a conclusion.

Use an estimate range, test a sale below the midpoint and update the evidence if the marketing period extends or the property condition changes.

chart.title: Example comparable sale prices
chart.note: Example sale prices produce a median of AED 1,700,000; use comparable transactions for a property valuation.

sections.heading: Use an index without confusing it with your unit
sections.body:
DLD's [residential sales price index](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/open-data/residential-properties-price-index-rppi/) describes a methodology designed to account for differences in residential property characteristics. An index can help understand a broader market period, but it does not price a specific apartment or replace building-level sales.

A change in the mix of transactions can affect simple averages. Compare the same property type, location and period, and check whether a series is revised. Do not apply a city-wide percentage mechanically to the purchase price of a single home.

Current competing listings can show what buyers see today. Track their asking prices and duration separately from completed transactions, since an advertisement can be changed or withdrawn.

sections.heading: Price and prepare the sale
sections.body:
Inspect the apartment, record the condition, check building charges and resolve questions about the title, mortgage or tenancy. A buyer may price uncertainty or required work into an offer. Obtain repair estimates and provide accurate information about the unit.

Estimate your net proceeds by deducting the outstanding loan, agreed selling costs and other obligations from a range of possible sale prices. The [mortgaged sale guide](/journal/how-to-sell-a-mortgaged-property-in-dubai) explains why a bank settlement quote and release process matter. Proceeds are not the same as profit.

Where a lender, authority or complex decision requires an independent valuation, use a provider and report accepted for that purpose. Ask about the report date, assumptions and limitations.

sections.heading: Revisit the price as evidence changes
sections.body:
Set a date to review the asking price alongside new completed sales, competing listings and feedback from qualified viewings. Ask whether a repeated objection concerns the layout, condition, building charges or the price. A slow response is useful information, but it does not by itself identify the correct discount.

Keep a written record of which comparables were used and what adjustments were made. If a stronger or more recent sale becomes available, update the range and discuss it with your adviser. The aim is a transparent decision based on current evidence, not a fixed number defended after its assumptions have changed.

sections.heading: Review a current apartment
sections.body:
Browse the [Aliyas Dubai project collection](/projects?emirate=Dubai) and [contact Aliyas](/contact) with the exact building, unit details and intended timing. Request a current market assessment and the source and date of comparable evidence. Check whether each comparison reflects a completed sale or an asking price and retain the details used to assess similarity.

Verify the transaction records and obtain an appropriate professional valuation when required before setting or accepting a price.

references.period: Official transaction filters and fields; checked 8 November 2026

aliyas-journal-155.excerpt: Compare Dubai and Ajman property investments using the complete purchase cost, ownership eligibility, owner expenses and net rental assumptions.
aliyas-journal-155.introduction:
A Dubai versus Ajman investment comparison should begin with two actual properties and the same definition of total cost. Add the price, registration, brokerage, finance and initial work, then estimate rent after vacancy and owner expenses. The cheapest headline price is not necessarily the lowest total cost or the best fit for your plans.

The examples below show how to compare acquisition costs using the same method. The examples provide a framework for comparing purchase costs across the two emirates.
takeaways: Verify your ownership right and obtain an itemised current quote for the exact property in each emirate.
Compare full acquisition cost and net operating income using the same period and expense categories.
Allow for building condition, finance, vacancy and eventual sale costs as well as the purchase price.

sections.heading: What does total purchase cost include?
sections.body:
Add the agreed price, buyer-paid registration and brokerage, applicable tax on services, any lender charges, inspection, repairs and furnishing. Keep a separate reserve for unexpected work or vacancy. Ask for written figures and confirm who pays each item.

For a completed Dubai property, DLD's [sale registration service](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/property-sale-registration/) lists 2% of the sale value for each party, plus other charges. The agreement can allocate the total differently. Ajman's [sale registration service](https://www.ajman.ae/en/servicecatalog/services/3162) lists its process and different fee categories; ask the department to clarify the current amount for the exact unit and buyer.

Do not apply one emirate's fee schedule to the other or assume the full cost from an advertised price. The [Dubai upfront cost guide](/journal/total-upfront-cost-of-buying-property-in-dubai) and [Ajman buying cost guide](/journal/total-cost-of-buying-an-apartment-in-ajman) explain the separate calculations.

table.caption: Compare the same cost categories
rows: Confirm the designated area and buyer's right
Confirm the right for this project and buyer
Comparable sales, fees and loan balance
Comparable sales, fees and loan balance

sections.heading: A sample cost comparison
sections.body:
Assume a sample Dubai apartment has a price of AED 1,000,000 and AED 55,000 of combined acquisition and setup costs, for a total of AED 1,055,000. Assume a sample Ajman apartment has a price of AED 650,000 and AED 30,000 of combined costs, for a total of AED 680,000. The difference is AED 375,000 in this example.

The two example homes differ in location, size, condition and tenant appeal. The example uses the same method for both locations so each cost can be compared consistently. The chart shows total entry cost before a separate contingency reserve.

Replace every input with an actual offer and current authority, broker, lender and repair quotes. Compare entry costs alongside rental income, vacancy and annual owner expenses.

chart.title: Example total acquisition and setup cost
chart.note: Sample prices and costs; the properties are not like-for-like market listings.

sections.heading: Verify eligibility and documents
sections.body:
Ask the relevant department to confirm the right available to your nationality for the exact unit. In Dubai, DLD's [FAQs](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/frequently-asked-questions) describe registration for non-UAE citizens in designated areas. In Ajman, verify the current project and buyer position with the land department; an older list of projects is not a substitute for a current confirmation.

Review title or initial registration, seller authority, developer clearance, any mortgage and an existing tenancy. For off-plan, check the project registration, contract, payment recipient, construction status and handover provisions. Keep receipts and the registered outcome.

If a representative will act for you, confirm the scope and validity of their authority and the documents required by the relevant service.

sections.heading: Compare net income and finance separately
sections.body:
Use recent signed leases for similar apartments in each building. Subtract a vacancy allowance and owner-paid service charges, management, repairs and insurance from expected rent. Divide by full acquisition cost to compare net operating yield. The [Dubai net yield guide](/journal/how-to-calculate-net-rental-yield-in-dubai) and [Ajman net yield guide](/journal/how-to-calculate-net-rental-yield-in-ajman) use the same principle.

If borrowing, prepare a separate repayment and cash-flow schedule. Compare lender fees, valuation, insurance and the remaining loan at sale; the loan offered for one property may differ from another. Do not present unleveraged operating yield as cash received after mortgage payments.

Test lower rent, longer vacancy and a major repair. A property should remain manageable without relying on a guaranteed tenant or resale gain.

sections.heading: Compare the building and the exit
sections.body:
Visit each unit and its common areas, check transport and services for the intended tenant, and request current service-charge and maintenance information. The [Ajman area guide](/journal/ajman-property-2026) and [Dubai Hills and Creek Harbour guide](/journal/dubai-hills-estate-vs-dubai-creek-harbour-for-families) provide location context, but individual buildings vary.

Seek recent completed sales of similar properties where evidence is available. Consider the time to sell, selling costs and any loan settlement. Use the emirate-wide total for context and compare completed sales for similar apartments.

Use the same holding period and risk assumptions where possible, and state what remains uncertain. A higher projected yield can accompany a different level of capital, management effort or resale risk.

sections.heading: Plan the timing of each payment
sections.body:
A cash buyer and a financed buyer may face different payment dates even when the purchase price is the same. Record the deposit, transfer charges, lender disbursement and any remaining instalments on a single calendar for each property. Check the refund conditions and whether a deposit is credited towards the price.

For an off-plan home, include the cost of your existing accommodation until the unit is ready and allow for a possible delay. For a ready rental investment, include the time and work needed before a tenant moves in. Compare the cash reserve left after each payment rather than only the total on paper.

sections.heading: Request current property details
sections.body:
Browse the [Aliyas Dubai projects](/projects?emirate=Dubai) and [Ajman projects](/projects?emirate=Ajman). [Contact Aliyas](/contact) with your budget, nationality and intended use, and ask which specific units are currently available.

Request written terms and verify the ownership right and official charges in the relevant emirate before making a commitment.

aliyas-journal-156.excerpt: Shortlist Sharjah family areas by comparing the actual home, school and work journeys, ownership eligibility and complete household budget.
aliyas-journal-156.introduction:
The best Sharjah area for a family is the one whose homes, school and work routes, services and total cost fit the household. Aljada, Al Mamsha and waterfront districts are useful starting points, but a community name cannot guarantee the layout, availability or ownership right of a particular property.

Visit the exact building or villa, test daily journeys and verify documents before deciding. This guide provides a comparison method rather than a universal ranking.
takeaways: Choose a shortlist around the family's actual school, work and space requirements.
Check which facilities are operating for the specific building and visit at useful times.
Confirm the buyer's ownership eligibility and full purchase and running costs with the relevant parties.

sections.heading: Which Sharjah settings should families compare?
sections.body:
[Arada's Aljada community page](https://www.arada.com/en/aljada/) describes a mixed development with homes and education, retail and leisure components. [Alef's Al Mamsha page](https://www.alefgroup.ae/alef-communities/almamsha/) describes an apartment community designed around pedestrian spaces and retail. Both are developer descriptions; check the specific phase and facilities currently open.

A family that values a waterfront setting can also examine suitable apartments in the Al Khan area. Compare the actual building, parking, access and available services rather than assuming an entire district has the same features. Ask schools about places and transport for your exact address.

The [Sharjah family living guide](/journal/sharjah-real-estate-family-living) provides wider context. Make a shortlist based on real homes, not a broad area label.

table.caption: Family shortlist: questions to investigate
rows: Phase, actual school place and daily routes
Title, condition, school and work travel

sections.heading: Test the family routine
sections.body:
List school, nursery, work, healthcare and the activities your family uses. Ask each school about admissions, year-group fees and transport for the exact address. Ask the school about admissions, fees and available places. Drive or use the intended transport route at the relevant time, including the return journey and any school pickup.

Consider the whole household, including people without a car. Check pavements, crossings, lift access and the route from parking to the apartment with a pushchair or other equipment if needed. Visit in the evening as well as during the day.

An advertised journey time or planned facility may not reflect current conditions. Record what you observe and ask about the status of services that are important to the family.

sections.heading: Inspect the home and its building
sections.body:
Check bedroom layout, storage, kitchen, laundry, cooling, windows and visible moisture. Measure spaces needed for existing furniture. Inspect the allocated parking, lifts, common areas and the actual pool or play area if these matter to you. Ask who maintains shared facilities and what is included in the charge.

For a ready home, arrange an appropriate inspection and record repairs to be completed or priced. For off-plan, review the signed specification, plan, payment schedule and handover terms. A rendering or show apartment is not necessarily the unit being purchased.

If a household member needs step-free access, test the route from the street or parking to the home rather than relying on the building description.

sections.heading: Verify ownership and the complete budget
sections.body:
Ask Sharjah's Real Estate Registration Department to confirm the ownership right available to your nationality for the exact property. [WAM's report of the 2022 Executive Council decision](https://www.wam.ae/en/article/hszrfs32-sharjah-executive-council-issues-decision-allowing) describes ownership in real estate development areas and projects; it does not mean every unit is automatically eligible.

Add the price, registration and brokerage, finance costs, service charges, insurance and any immediate work. Request an itemised current quote and keep a separate reserve. For an apartment, ask for the current unit statement and the scope of building services.

Check the title or initial registration, seller authority, any mortgage or tenancy and required clearance. Obtain qualified advice where the documentation or contract is unclear.

sections.heading: Use a family scorecard
sections.body:
Set non-negotiables first, such as the number of bedrooms, an acceptable school route and a documented ownership right. Then score remaining homes on layout, travel, affordability and facilities using your viewing notes. The chart shows one sample set of priorities, not ratings of Sharjah neighbourhoods.

Confirm school availability and service charges before choosing a home for your family. Revisit the most important uncertainty before committing. A second visit may be more valuable than a higher score based only on a brochure.

chart.title: Example family home priorities
chart.note: Sample weights total 100 points and do not rate any area.

sections.heading: Compare apartment and villa running costs
sections.body:
A villa can offer a different layout and outdoor area from an apartment, but it may also have different cooling, garden, parking and maintenance responsibilities. Request recent bills where available and ask which costs are covered by community charges. Past bills are useful context rather than a guarantee of your family's consumption.

For an apartment, examine the building's management, the approved charge and the condition of shared facilities. For both property types, include school transport, insurance and commuting in the annual household plan. An affordable purchase price still needs to leave room for these recurring obligations and an emergency reserve.

sections.heading: Compare a lease with a purchase
sections.body:
If you are also considering renting, compare a similar home over the same expected stay. A lease can provide flexibility but has its own payment, deposit, renewal and notice terms. A purchase involves transaction costs and the risk that the eventual sale price changes. Ask for the complete agreement and current official registration process for either choice.

Use your budget to shortlist homes that match your family’s priorities and preferred location. Ask for current options, inspect them and replace assumptions with written figures before choosing.

sections.heading: Explore current family homes
sections.body:
Browse the [Aliyas Sharjah project collection](/projects?emirate=Sharjah) and ask which specific homes are currently available. Request the exact address, plan, price, ownership documentation and current charges.

[Contact Aliyas](/contact) with your family size, preferred schools, work destinations and budget. Verify eligibility and visit the home before committing.

aliyas-journal-157.excerpt: Read Sharjah's 2027 property outlook through the latest available transaction, approved-project and supply evidence, with clear limits on forecasts.
aliyas-journal-157.introduction:
Sharjah's 2027 property outlook depends on the balance between demand, new supply, financing and the performance of individual projects. The latest official department figures reported by Emirates News Agency for this guide cover the first nine months of 2026. They show real estate activity across the emirate during the stated period.

Use the dated evidence to frame questions, then inspect the specific property, ownership right, cost and competing supply. Update this outlook as newer official data becomes available.
takeaways: Sharjah reported AED 46.8 billion in mixed real estate transactions in January–September 2026, not apartment sales alone.
Approved ownership projects and new supply require unit-specific verification and can change over time.
Build scenarios for rent, vacancy, financing and resale instead of treating a 2027 outcome as certain.

sections.heading: What does the latest official activity show?
sections.body:
[Emirates News Agency's October 2026 report](https://www.wam.ae/en/article/c2q0o4j-sharjah-real-estate-transactions-hit-aed-468bn), citing Sharjah's Real Estate Registration Department, reports AED 46.8 billion in monetary transaction volume from January to September 2026, compared with AED 44.3 billion in the same period of 2025. The report states growth of 5.6%.

It reports 91,560 total transactions in the 2026 period and separately discusses title deeds, preliminary contracts and mortgages. These categories and the monetary total are not the same as completed sales of comparable apartments. Compare the broad figures with property-level prices, rent and owner costs.

The chart compares the two reported nine-month monetary totals. The periods and measure match, but the mix of property and transaction types can still change.

chart.title: Sharjah real estate monetary transaction volume
chart.note: WAM, 13 October 2026, citing the Sharjah department. Totals cover mixed transaction and property types, not apartment sales alone.

table.caption: Dated evidence and its limits
rows: AED 46.8bn in the first nine months of 2026
Not the number of apartment sales
Does not confirm a particular unit's eligibility
Supply, demand and prices remain uncertain

sections.heading: How should buyers read ownership and supply?
sections.body:
A [separate WAM report](https://www.wam.ae/en/article/c2qm3mo-sharjah-real-estate-attracts-9891-new-investors) says 52 projects had been approved for freehold ownership by non-citizens and foreign investors since the 2022 resolution, as reported in October 2026. The count can change and does not establish that every property is eligible. Ask the Sharjah Real Estate Registration Department to confirm the right for the buyer and exact unit.

Review the registered project, developer, contract, construction status and scheduled competing supply near a shortlisted property. A planned handover can move, and the number of announced units does not tell you how many will be vacant at the same time.

For a ready apartment, inspect the building and obtain the current service-charge statement. For off-plan, map the complete instalment schedule and verify the relevant registration and payment process.

sections.heading: What might influence demand in 2027?
sections.body:
Household needs, employment, access to schools and work, financing costs and the alternatives available in neighbouring emirates can all influence demand. Their impact differs across family villas, apartments and individual communities. Broad transaction activity cannot predict the rent or value of one home.

Seek recent signed leases and completed sales for comparable units where available. Distinguish an asking price from a completed transaction and record the date and terms. A tenant's actual route and building facilities can matter more than an emirate-wide average.

The [Sharjah family living guide](/journal/sharjah-real-estate-family-living) and [family-area shortlist](/journal/best-areas-to-buy-property-in-sharjah-for-families) provide location context. Visit the exact property and verify current services.

sections.heading: Prepare a range of scenarios
sections.body:
A stronger scenario might involve stable demand and timely project delivery. A weaker scenario could include longer vacancy, higher owner charges or competing new homes. These are planning possibilities, not predictions or probabilities. Calculate each using your own purchase and lease evidence.

For a rental investment, subtract vacancy, service charges, management, repairs and insurance from expected rent before comparing it with full acquisition cost. Keep financing and eventual sale costs separate. For an owner-occupied home, test the mortgage payment, school and transport budget and any delay to moving.

Maintain a reserve for an unexpected repair or income change. A purchase that depends on a particular 2027 price increase is exposed to an outcome no current report can guarantee.

sections.heading: What should you check before buying?
sections.body:
Confirm the buyer's eligibility, title or initial registration, seller authority, mortgage or tenancy and any required developer clearance. Request a written quote for official and transaction costs, and ask which party pays each item. For a new development, review the specification, payment schedule, handover and default provisions.

Compare the actual location and unit with genuine alternatives. A city-wide increase in activity can coexist with weaker demand or higher costs in a particular building. Ask for current building charges and evidence for the intended use.

Refresh the official data, project status and fees before publication or purchase. A title referring to 2027 should not imply that a future result is already known.

sections.heading: Watch affordability and delivery through 2027
sections.body:
Track the timing of actual handovers against previously announced schedules and check how much competing supply is similar to the property you are considering. Review signed rents and completed sales where accessible, noting their dates and unit characteristics. A change in the number of transactions may reflect a change in the mix of property types as well as demand.

If using finance, request a current bank offer and stress-test the repayment against your income and reserve. Interest rates, eligibility and valuations can change. Keep a record of the assumptions and revisit the decision when a material cost or project milestone changes.

sections.heading: Explore current Sharjah projects
sections.body:
Browse the [Aliyas Sharjah project collection](/projects?emirate=Sharjah) and [contact Aliyas](/contact) with your budget, nationality and intended use. Ask which specific units are currently available and request their documents, price and payment terms. Compare the evidence for each option on the same basis and keep the date of every quotation.

Verify the ownership right and current official requirements before committing.

aliyas-journal-158.excerpt: Check foreign ownership eligibility in Sharjah by confirming the buyer, exact project, type of right and registration with the relevant authority.
aliyas-journal-158.introduction:
Foreign ownership eligibility in Sharjah must be checked for the specific buyer and property. The emirate has approved real estate development areas and projects for ownership by non-citizens, but an advertisement or a general area name does not establish the right available for every unit. Ask Sharjah's Real Estate Registration Department to confirm the current status before paying.

This guide explains the evidence to request and the limits of published project counts. Rules, approved projects and transaction requirements can change; verify the current position for your circumstances.
takeaways: Confirm the exact project, unit, buyer's nationality and type of registered right with the Sharjah authority.
The 2022 decision reported by WAM concerns ownership in real estate development areas and projects, not an automatic right over every property.
Review the title or initial registration, seller authority, clearance and current transaction charges.

sections.heading: What did the 2022 decision say?
sections.body:
[Emirates News Agency reported](https://www.wam.ae/en/article/hszrfs32-sharjah-executive-council-issues-decision-allowing) that Sharjah's Executive Council issued a decision in November 2022 allowing all nationalities to own real estate without a time limit in real estate development areas and projects, following a change to the registration law. The scope and current application must be confirmed for the property and buyer.

A separate [WAM report on the amended registration law](https://www.wam.ae/en/article/hszrfrop-sharjah-ruler-amends-law-no-5-real-estate) describes ownership in development areas and projects under the council's regulations. It also describes other categories of ownership. Do not assume that all categories and rights have identical conditions.

Ask whether the interest is freehold, usufruct or another right, who can acquire it and how it will be registered. Use the sales brochure to identify the property and check its ownership terms with the authority.

table.caption: Eligibility questions for the exact property
rows: Current confirmation from the registration department
Title or initial registration showing the type of interest
Confirmation for the buyer's nationality and circumstances
Seller authority, mortgage and clearance documents
Current process, charges and expected ownership document

sections.heading: Why must the project list be checked again?
sections.body:
WAM reports citing the Sharjah department described 47 approved projects by the end of Q1 2026, 50 by the end of H1 and 52 by the end of September. These are cumulative counts at different dates, not numbers to add together. They demonstrate that the reported list changed during the year.

The chart plots those reported checkpoints. A project count does not identify whether your unit is eligible, and it can become outdated. Request current confirmation from the department, including any conditions for the exact buyer and property.

The [Q1 report](https://www.wam.ae/en/article/bzpnrud-sharjah-real-estate-increases-407-reaching-aed185), [H1 report](https://www.wam.ae/en/article/c18fnby-sharjah-real-estate-transactions-reach-aed295) and [nine-month report](https://www.wam.ae/en/article/c2qm3mo-sharjah-real-estate-attracts-9891-new-investors) describe the respective counts.

chart.title: Reported approved-project checkpoints in 2026
chart.note: WAM reports citing the Sharjah department. Counts are cumulative and must not be added; verify the current list.

sections.heading: How do you verify the unit?
sections.body:
Record the project name, registration details, building, unit number and seller or developer. Ask the department which documents it needs to confirm the buyer's right. Compare the official title or initial registration with the sale agreement and the identity and authority of the seller.

For a ready unit, check any mortgage, existing lease, building charges and required developer or management clearance. For an off-plan unit, review the registered project, contract, payment recipient, instalments and handover terms. Seek advice if the right being offered or a transfer condition is unclear.

The [Sharjah family area guide](/journal/best-areas-to-buy-property-in-sharjah-for-families) provides location context, but an area guide does not establish ownership eligibility for a particular apartment.

sections.heading: Check registration and costs
sections.body:
Ask the registration department and developer for an itemised current quote, the required documents, the parties responsible for each charge and the expected registration outcome. The Sharjah Executive Council's [property sale service listing](https://ec.shj.ae/en/government-service-details?serviceId=7804877f29e1d98d856134f4180a0517ef859c39c3ca891bc3a13e3773b7316bf5fcd08d2966872ceec3e0acf29842ff) describes a title transfer service; confirm its current applicability to the unit.

Do not apply a promotional exhibition rate or a fee quoted for another nationality to your transaction without confirmation. Add brokerage, finance, inspection and initial work where relevant, and keep a separate contingency.

If using a representative, check the required authority, notarisation and any translation. Verify payment instructions independently and retain receipts and the issued registration document.

sections.heading: What if the information is unclear?
sections.body:
Ask the authority for clarification before paying a reservation amount. Record the project and unit identifiers used in the enquiry and keep the response with the contract. If the seller's documents and official information disagree, resolve the discrepancy before proceeding.

A property purchase, a mortgage approval and a residence visa are separate decisions. Do not assume one automatically establishes the others. For legal or cross-border tax questions, consult an appropriately qualified adviser with the actual documents.

Review the confirmation if the buyer, property or transaction structure changes. A right verified for one unit or nationality should not be transferred to a different case without a new check.

sections.heading: Questions for the developer and registration department
sections.body:
Ask the developer for the project's official registration details and a copy of the unit's relevant ownership or initial-registration document. Confirm whether the seller is the registered holder and whether any instalment, mortgage or clearance remains outstanding. Take the exact identifiers to the department when checking eligibility.

Ask the department how the buyer's identity should be recorded, whether an authorised representative may sign and what documentation is required for the particular ownership right. If buying through a company, seek advice on the company's eligibility and registration rather than assuming the rules for an individual apply unchanged. Keep the answer and the date it was obtained.

sections.heading: Distinguish eligibility from availability
sections.body:
An approved development can contain many different units and phases. Approval of a project does not mean that the apartment shown in an advertisement is available, that its price is current or that the seller can transfer it immediately. Confirm the exact unit and the current contract position independently.

For an off-plan home, review the instalment schedule and delivery terms as well as ownership. For a ready home, inspect the condition and building costs. Eligibility is a necessary check, but it is only one part of the purchase decision.

sections.heading: Request current Sharjah options
sections.body:
Browse the [Aliyas Sharjah project collection](/projects?emirate=Sharjah) and [contact Aliyas](/contact) with your nationality, budget and intended use. Ask which units are currently available and request the project and registration details.

Confirm the current ownership right and official charges with the relevant Sharjah authority before committing.

aliyas-journal-159.excerpt: Build a complete Sharjah apartment purchase budget, including registration, brokerage, financing, initial work and a separate reserve.
aliyas-journal-159.introduction:
The total cost of buying an apartment in Sharjah includes more than the advertised price. Registration and other charges depend on the buyer, property, transaction and agreement, so obtain an itemised current quote from the relevant authority and providers. Include finance, initial work and ongoing building costs in the decision.

The example in this guide uses sample amounts to demonstrate a budget. The calculation provides a practical worksheet for the apartment and purchase terms you choose.
takeaways: Confirm the buyer's ownership right and the current property-specific registration quote before paying.
Add brokerage, finance, inspection and initial work to the agreed price, and keep a separate reserve.
Compare ongoing service charges and mortgage payments as well as the initial cash required.

sections.heading: Which costs should you identify?
sections.body:
Ask for the agreed unit price, registration and title charges, developer or management clearance, brokerage, any tax on services and the party responsible for each item. For a financed purchase, add valuation, bank fees, insurance and the timing of the loan. For a ready apartment, obtain estimates for inspection and immediate work.

The Sharjah Executive Council's [property sale service listing](https://ec.shj.ae/en/government-service-details?serviceId=7804877f29e1d98d856134f4180a0517ef859c39c3ca891bc3a13e3773b7316bf5fcd08d2966872ceec3e0acf29842ff) describes a title transfer service. Ask Sharjah's registration department for the current process and itemised fee quote for your exact unit and nationality.

Promotional terms for a particular event or project are not a universal schedule. Check whether an incentive applies to your unit and whether its conditions are recorded in the contract.

rows: Signed unit-specific price and payment schedule
Current authority quote and allocation between parties
Written fees, tax and required approvals
Down payment, valuation, lender fees and insurance

sections.heading: Work through a sample budget
sections.body:
Suppose an apartment costs AED 800,000, registration and related charges are assumed at AED 40,000, brokerage at AED 16,000, finance costs at AED 9,000 and immediate repairs at AED 10,000. The total is AED 875,000 before a separate contingency reserve and other ongoing expenses.

These example amounts show how the different purchase costs contribute to the total budget. The chart separates the example components. An actual transaction may have different charges, allocation, tax, insurance and payment timing.

A mortgage reduces the price paid in cash at transfer but creates repayments and a balance outstanding. Prepare a separate cash-flow schedule using the bank's actual offer; the total property cost is not the same as the initial down payment.

chart.title: Example purchase cost before contingency
chart.note: Sample assumptions total AED 875,000; actual fees and other costs must be quoted.

sections.heading: Confirm the ownership right and registration
sections.body:
[WAM's report of Sharjah's 2022 ownership decision](https://www.wam.ae/en/article/hszrfs32-sharjah-executive-council-issues-decision-allowing) describes ownership by all nationalities in real estate development areas and projects. Confirm eligibility for the exact apartment and buyer with the relevant authority. Ask the registration department to confirm the right for your nationality and exact unit.

Review the title or initial registration, seller authority, any mortgage or lease and required developer clearance. For an off-plan purchase, confirm the registered project, payment recipient, contract and instalments. The [Sharjah ownership eligibility guide](/journal/how-to-check-foreign-ownership-eligibility-in-sharjah) explains the questions to ask.

Verify payment instructions through independently confirmed contacts and keep the official registration outcome and receipts. A reservation receipt alone is not a title deed.

sections.heading: Plan cash and finance timing
sections.body:
Record each deposit, instalment, bank disbursement and fee due date on a calendar. Confirm whether a booking amount is credited towards the price and when it may be refunded. Do not count the same payment twice.

Ask the lender for the loan amount, valuation, interest or profit rate, fees, insurance and repayment schedule. Approval and financing depend on the applicant and property. Test a smaller loan or delayed approval, and maintain cash for the difference.

For off-plan, include the full handover and any later balance. A low first instalment does not make the remaining obligation disappear. Allow for continued rent or other housing costs until the home is ready.

sections.heading: Budget for ownership after purchase
sections.body:
Request the current unit service-charge statement, payment schedule, building management contact and any arrears or major work information. Ask what utilities and cooling are billed separately. Include insurance, maintenance and a reserve for repairs inside the apartment.

For a rental investment, allow for vacancy and the owner's management costs. Compare recent signed leases for similar units rather than treating an advertised yield as a guarantee. For a family home, include school transport and commuting in the household budget.

The [Sharjah family area guide](/journal/best-areas-to-buy-property-in-sharjah-for-families) helps compare locations, but costs and facilities vary by building and unit.

sections.heading: Compare ready and off-plan quotations
sections.body:
A ready apartment may need a larger payment at transfer and immediate repair work. An off-plan unit may spread the price across several dates, but the later payments remain due under the agreement. Request the full schedule and an itemised quote for both; a smaller booking payment is not the total purchase cost.

Ask which authority and developer charges are payable at reservation, registration and handover. If an incentive covers a fee, confirm the conditions and whether it reduces the amount you would otherwise pay. Do not assume that a promotional payment plan includes every transaction charge.

sections.heading: Keep a separate contingency
sections.body:
A reserve is money set aside for future expenses and kept separate from official fees. Consider a repair, a delayed handover or a smaller mortgage approval and check whether the purchase remains affordable. If you must pay rent during construction, include that on the cash calendar.

Update the budget when a written quotation or lender valuation changes. A subtotal that excludes an unknown charge should be clearly marked as incomplete until the amount and responsible party are confirmed.

sections.heading: Request a property-specific quote
sections.body:
Browse the [Aliyas Sharjah project collection](/projects?emirate=Sharjah) and [contact Aliyas](/contact) with your nationality, budget and intended use. Ask which units are currently available and request the exact plan, price and written cost breakdown.

Confirm eligibility and current authority charges before making a payment.

aliyas-journal-160.excerpt: Compare buying an apartment in Aljada and Al Mamsha using the actual building, layout, ownership documents, payment schedule and total cost.
aliyas-journal-160.introduction:
Aljada and Al Mamsha both offer Sharjah apartment buyers a community setting, but the better purchase depends on the individual building, phase and household needs. Compare the exact unit's layout, access, operating facilities, ownership right and full cost rather than deciding from the masterplan alone.

The example costs below show a consistent method for comparing the two homes. The examples show how purchase costs can be compared using the same approach for each home.
takeaways: Inspect the exact building and distinguish completed facilities from planned phases.
Confirm the buyer's ownership eligibility and request the full payment and registration schedule.
Compare total cost, service charges, daily journeys and the apartment's condition on the same basis.

sections.heading: How do the communities compare?
sections.body:
[Arada describes Aljada](https://www.arada.com/en/aljada/) as a mixed community with residential, education, retail and leisure components. [Alef describes Al Mamsha](https://www.alefgroup.ae/alef-communities/almamsha/) as an apartment community designed around pedestrian spaces, retail and leisure. These are developer descriptions; check the status and access of the particular phase and building.

Walk the route from the apartment entrance to parking, shops and any facility you plan to use. Check whether the school, pool or other amenity is currently operating and whether it serves your building. Check which facilities are complete and available to residents of the chosen home.

The [Sharjah family area guide](/journal/best-areas-to-buy-property-in-sharjah-for-families) offers a wider shortlist if other locations may suit the household.

rows: Inspect the unit, parking and building

sections.heading: Inspect the apartment and phase
sections.body:
Check the layout, usable storage, kitchen, cooling, windows, noise and visible condition. Measure the spaces needed for furniture. Confirm the allocated parking and the route from it to the unit. If buying off-plan, compare the signed plan and specification with the sales material and ask for dated construction progress.

Review the building management, common areas, service-charge statement and any outstanding balance. Ask which shared facilities are included in the charge and how faults are reported. Two buildings in the same community may have different costs and maintenance histories.

For a ready apartment, arrange an appropriate inspection and record any agreed repairs. For an off-plan unit, check the handover, delay and specification-change provisions with a qualified adviser if necessary.

sections.heading: Compare the complete cost
sections.body:
Imagine an Aljada apartment priced at AED 850,000 with AED 40,000 of assumed acquisition costs and AED 10,000 of setup work, totalling AED 900,000. A sample Al Mamsha apartment costs AED 820,000 with AED 55,000 of assumed acquisition costs and AED 20,000 of setup, totalling AED 895,000. The example figures show how the purchase costs are organised for each home.

The chart shows these example totals before a separate contingency and ongoing charges. A lower asking price does not necessarily remain lower after the other inputs. Replace every number with a written quote for the actual unit.

The [Sharjah purchase cost guide](/journal/total-cost-of-buying-an-apartment-in-sharjah) explains the categories to include. If borrowing, compare the bank's down payment, fees, repayment schedule and insurance separately.

sections.heading: Check ownership and registration
sections.body:
Ask Sharjah's registration department to confirm the right available to your nationality for the exact unit and project. The [Sharjah ownership eligibility guide](/journal/how-to-check-foreign-ownership-eligibility-in-sharjah) explains the documents and questions. Developer marketing alone does not confirm the current legal position for every property.

Review the title or initial registration, seller or developer authority, any mortgage or tenancy and required clearance. Obtain a written quote for registration, brokerage and other transaction costs. Verify the payment recipient independently and retain receipts and registration documents.

For an off-plan purchase, review the instalment dates, specification, handover and default terms. Review the full purchase price and the dates of all remaining instalments.

sections.heading: Test the household routine and future use
sections.body:
Take the school and work routes at the times you would actually travel. Ask schools about places and transport for the exact address. Check whether the household needs a second car or paid parking and include that cost. A planned connection is not the same as a service operating today.

If the apartment is an investment, seek recent signed leases for comparable units and deduct vacancy, service charges, management and repairs. Do not treat an area-wide advertised yield as a guarantee. If it is a family home, compare storage, play space and accessibility as well as cost.

Keep a reserve and test a delay or unexpected repair. Consider whether the apartment will remain suitable if the household or work routine changes.

sections.heading: Compare payment timing
sections.body:
Put the deposit, registration, construction instalments, handover balance and any bank disbursement on a calendar. Include current rent until the new home is available. Confirm whether a reservation amount is credited towards the price and the written conditions for a refund.

A payment plan can make two prices appear similar while creating very different cash needs at handover. Compare the full schedule and retain enough liquidity for an unexpected delay or change in financing. Do not rely on an assumed future sale to meet a contractual payment.

Ask when a final service-charge budget will be available for a new building and whether the estimate is approved or preliminary. Add the anticipated annual amount to the household or investment worksheet, and update it once the actual statement is issued.

aliyas-journal-161.excerpt: Compare Masaar and Al Zahia villas for family living by inspecting the home, school and work routes, community costs and ownership documents.
aliyas-journal-161.introduction:
Masaar and Al Zahia offer different Sharjah family settings. A villa in either community should be judged by its exact phase, layout, condition, daily journeys and full cost. A woodland plan or a nearby mall can be attractive, but neither guarantees the right home for every household.

Use the developer descriptions as starting points, then visit the property and check the facilities, ownership position and current terms for the specific villa.
takeaways: Compare the actual villa and phase, including usable rooms, parking, maintenance and outdoor space.
Test school and work journeys at the times your family will travel.
Verify ownership eligibility, community charges and the complete purchase and running costs.

sections.heading: What is different about the settings?
sections.body:
[Arada describes Masaar](https://www.arada.com/en/masaar/) as a community of villas and townhouses arranged around a green spine in Al Suyoh. [Al Zahia's community site](https://www.alzahia.ae/en) describes neighbourhoods with apartments, townhouses and villas and access to City Centre Al Zahia. These are developer descriptions, not proof that every facility is open or included for a particular home.

Check the exact phase and street, distance to the facilities you will use, parking and any ongoing construction. Ask which parts are operating now and what is still planned. A woodland view or mall access should be verified from the actual villa and route.

The [Sharjah family area guide](/journal/best-areas-to-buy-property-in-sharjah-for-families) provides a broader shortlist if other settings may also fit your family.

sections.heading: Inspect the villa and plot
sections.body:
Check bedroom placement, bathrooms, kitchen, storage, laundry and stairs. Consider the needs of children or older relatives and measure rooms for existing furniture. Inspect the garden, boundary, gate, drainage and allocated parking. Ask which appliances and fixtures are included.

Test cooling, water pressure, doors and windows where safe and permitted. Look for visible leaks or cracks, request maintenance records and obtain a qualified inspection for significant defects. If the villa has an extension or alteration, verify approvals and whether it matches the property records.

For an off-plan home, review the signed specification, plan, payment dates and handover terms. A show villa may not have the same layout or finish as the unit in the contract.

sections.heading: Test school and work journeys
sections.body:
List the actual school, nursery, workplace and healthcare destinations. Ask schools about admission, fees and transport for the exact address. Test the route at departure and return times, including school pickup. Test the commute from the entrance you would use at your usual travel times.

Check what happens if a car is unavailable and whether a second vehicle or school bus is needed. Visit on a working day and in the evening to assess access, noise and the household routine. Record the time and conditions rather than relying on an advertised drive time.

If a facility or road is planned, check its current status with the provider. Make sure the family can manage if delivery changes.

sections.heading: Compare all costs and ownership
sections.body:
Add the purchase price, buyer-paid registration and brokerage, lender fees, inspection and initial work. Request the current community charge, what it covers and any arrears. Include cooling, garden upkeep, insurance, school transport and commuting in an annual household budget. Keep a separate reserve for unexpected repairs.

Ask Sharjah's registration department to confirm the right available to your nationality for the exact villa. The [Sharjah ownership guide](/journal/how-to-check-foreign-ownership-eligibility-in-sharjah) explains how to check project approval, title and transfer. Review any mortgage, tenancy or developer clearance and obtain an itemised current quote.

If financing, compare the actual bank offer and payment calendar. A property should remain affordable after the down payment as well as on the day of purchase.

sections.heading: Use a family decision scorecard
sections.body:
Set non-negotiables for bedrooms, budget, legal eligibility and a workable school route. Score the remaining villas on evidence from the viewing. The chart shows one sample set of weights: layout and condition 35 points, travel 30, affordability 25 and community facilities 10. It does not rate Masaar or Al Zahia.

Mark unresolved questions, such as a school place or community charge, rather than treating them as favourable. Revisit the villa or seek documents before finalising a choice. The most suitable setting is the one that works for the household's actual routine and reserve.

sections.heading: Check the community rules
sections.body:
Ask about visitor access, maintenance, permitted exterior changes, pets and the process for reporting a shared-area fault. If a clubhouse or pool matters, verify who can use it and whether a separate fee applies. A facility in the wider masterplan is not necessarily included in every villa's terms.

Request the management contact and any available charge history or information about planned work. Keep the documents with your comparison so the family's expectations match the obligations attached to the home.

Walk from the villa to the spaces your family expects to use and check crossings, lighting and access with children or a pushchair. Ask how residents are notified about maintenance or temporary closures. These practical details can differ between phases even when the community name is the same.

sections.body:
Browse the [Aliyas Sharjah project collection](/projects?emirate=Sharjah) and ask which specific Masaar or Al Zahia homes are currently available. [Contact Aliyas](/contact) with your budget, bedrooms and school and work destinations. Keep a comparison sheet for each villa you view.

Request the exact address, plan, price, community charges and ownership documents, then verify official requirements before committing.

Muwaileh and Al Khan offer different Sharjah apartment settings, but the right purchase depends on the specific building and your intended use. Compare the home, route to work or school, ownership documents, service charges and total purchase cost before deciding.

Use area descriptions alongside the apartment’s condition, ownership terms and costs. The worked figures below show how the two homes can be compared on the same basis.
takeaways: Check the specific building, phase and daily routes in each location.

Use comparable signed leases or completed sales where available, and include owner expenses.

[Bayut's Muwaileh guide](https://www.bayut.com/area-guides/muwaileh/) describes an area associated with residential buildings and education facilities. Its [Al Khan guide](https://www.bayut.com/area-guides/al-khan-sharjah/) describes a waterfront district with apartment towers. These broad descriptions do not establish the location, view or condition of an individual unit.

In Muwaileh, identify the exact project and phase and check the route to the services you use. In Al Khan, check the building's position, parking and actual access to the waterfront. Visit at the time you would normally travel and again in the evening if possible.

The [Sharjah family area guide](/journal/best-areas-to-buy-property-in-sharjah-for-families) provides a wider shortlist; use the actual property documents and viewing to make the final comparison.

sections.heading: Consider the daily routine or tenant
sections.body:
For a family home, test the actual routes to school, work and healthcare and check school admission and transport for the address. Ask about utility, cooling and community costs. A shorter distance on a map may not mean a convenient journey at the required time.

For a rental investment, seek recent signed leases for similar apartments and subtract vacancy, owner charges, management, insurance and repairs. Compare the resulting net income with total acquisition cost. An advertised yield is not evidence of income collected from this unit.

Review nearby scheduled handovers and competing homes, but do not infer future vacancy or capital growth from a project count alone.

sections.heading: Plan the exit and reserve
sections.body:
Seek recent completed sales of similar units where available and keep asking prices separate. Include selling charges and any loan settlement in a future proceeds estimate. A view, building condition and tenancy can affect the comparison, so record the details behind each sale.

Keep a reserve for an unexpected repair or vacancy. If borrowing, test the repayment schedule and a lower valuation or delayed approval. Choose the property that remains manageable under a less favourable scenario, not only the one with the most attractive headline figure.

Ask how long comparable units have been offered and whether the evidence reflects a completed transaction. A small sample or an older sale may be a weak basis for a precise valuation. Seek an appropriate professional assessment when the lender or the decision requires one.

aliyas-journal-163.introduction:
Al Majaz and Al Taawun both have Sharjah apartment buildings that may suit families, but the best rental depends on the exact tower, household routine and lease. Inspect the home, test the school and work journeys and compare the full cost rather than choosing solely by the area name.

The figures below show how a household can compare rental costs over the same period. The calculation uses a consistent set of inputs to compare the two rental choices.
takeaways: Compare the apartment layout, building condition and actual route to the family's destinations.
Include utilities, transport, non-refundable charges and move-in deposits alongside annual rent.
Review the written lease and confirm the current Sharjah attestation process.

sections.heading: How do the areas differ?
sections.body:
[Bayut's Al Majaz guide](https://www.bayut.com/area-guides/al-majaz/) describes apartment buildings around the Khaled Lagoon and Buhaira Corniche. Its [Al Taawun guide](https://www.bayut.com/area-guides/al-taawun/) describes a district near the Sharjah–Dubai border with apartment towers and local services. Both descriptions are broad; check the precise building, parking and street.

Visit the building at school and work departure times as well as in the evening. Walk from the entrance to the services the family will use and check crossings, lift access and space for a pushchair if relevant. Inspect the outlook from the specific apartment and its outdoor areas.

The [Sharjah family living guide](/journal/sharjah-real-estate-family-living) provides wider context for the household's location search.

The chart covers only rent, utilities and transport. Add school transport, parking, insurance, non-refundable fees and other differences for your household. Treat refundable deposits as cash needed at move-in and record any eventual deduction separately.

A lower annual amount may not be the best choice if the layout or travel time does not work. Compare homes of similar size and condition and use written terms.

sections.heading: Inspect the apartment and building
sections.body:
Check the bedroom layout, storage, kitchen, cooling, water pressure, windows and visible moisture. Confirm the allocated parking and access from it to the apartment. Ask whether cooling or any utilities are included, how they are billed and who handles repairs.

Inspect lifts, corridors, entry controls and the condition of shared facilities. If a pool or play area matters, confirm it serves the building and is currently operating. Ask about noise and visit at a second time if possible.

Agree a dated condition record and furniture inventory where relevant. Record existing marks and repairs before moving in, and retain a copy with the lease and receipts.

sections.heading: Check school and work journeys
sections.body:
Ask the school about places, fees and bus service for the exact address. Test the journey from the home at the time of the actual school run, including the return. If an adult commutes to Dubai, test the entire route rather than assuming an area near the border is fastest for every workplace.

Include fuel, parking, tolls or public transport and any second vehicle in the budget. Check alternatives for days when the usual route or car is unavailable. The time and cost for other household members to reach shops and healthcare also matter.

A map or advertised travel time is a starting point. Actual access depends on the building entrance, route and time of day.

sections.heading: Read and attest the lease
sections.body:
Request the full rent schedule, security deposit, brokerage and other charges, maintenance responsibilities, renewal, notice and early-exit terms. Verify the landlord or representative's authority and the payment recipient. Ask how the deposit will be assessed and returned.

Sharjah Municipality's [residential tenancy contract template](https://portal.shjmun.gov.ae/en/eservices/Attachements/Residential-Tenancy-Contract-Template.pdf) describes attestation and the parties' obligations under the referenced law. Confirm the current procedure, deadline and charges with the municipality for your agreement; do not rely on an old fee quoted elsewhere.

Keep the attested contract, receipts, meter readings and inventory. Obtain qualified advice if a clause or the responsibilities are unclear.

sections.heading: Plan the move-in cash
sections.body:
Put the first rent payment, deposit, non-refundable fees, utility connection, moving and furniture on a calendar. Ask whether the building requires a move-in permit or refundable deposit and confirm its return conditions. A deposit may be returned later but still reduces the cash available at the start.

Record the remaining rent instalments and school payments as well. If two large payments fall in the same month, plan for them before signing. Keep a reserve for unexpected household costs.

Ask which utility accounts must be opened and whether the previous balance has been settled. Confirm the connection date and any deposit with the provider. If the home is furnished, agree the inventory and condition of appliances so that the move-in record matches what the family actually receives.

sections.body:
Browse the [Aliyas Sharjah project collection](/projects?emirate=Sharjah) for local context and ask which relevant Al Majaz or Al Taawun rentals are currently available. Ask for the lease terms and the current availability of the apartment you want to view.

[Contact Aliyas](/contact) with your budget, bedrooms and school or work destinations. Request the exact address and written terms, then view the actual apartment.

A building with a desirable position may have a different price or charge from another project. Test an unexpected repair, a delayed handover or a longer vacancy. Keep sufficient cash after the purchase and ask whether your plans would still work under a less favourable scenario.

Ask how the community is managed, whether a particular pool or beach access is included and how residents report a fault. Check service-charge statements and building rules before attributing a benefit to every apartment. Charge statement, quotes and comparable signed leases
Comparable completed sales, selling costs and loan balance

sections.heading: 2. Inspect the unit and maintenance
sections.body:
Check windows, seals, balconies, cooling, plumbing and visible moisture. Ask about the condition and maintenance of exposed fittings and common areas. Coastal exposure can affect maintenance needs, but it should be assessed for the individual building rather than assumed to have caused damage.

Request the service-charge statement, maintenance history, management contact and information about any known major work. Ask which insurance is held for shared areas and what cover the owner needs for the apartment. Obtain a qualified inspection if there are concerns about water ingress, corrosion or another technical issue.

For an off-plan unit, review the signed specification, completion and handover provisions. Check the project's current status and payment process with the relevant authority and developer.

sections.heading: 3. Verify ownership and transaction costs
sections.body:
Ask Sharjah's registration department to confirm the buyer's right for the exact property. Review title or initial registration, seller authority, any mortgage or tenancy and required clearance. The [Sharjah eligibility guide](/journal/how-to-check-foreign-ownership-eligibility-in-sharjah) explains the evidence to request.

Obtain an itemised current quote for registration, brokerage, finance and other charges. Add initial work and furnishing to the price, and keep a separate reserve. Do not assume a fee or ownership right applies to every waterfront project.

Verify payment instructions independently and keep receipts and the official registration outcome. Seek qualified advice if the documents or contractual obligations are unclear.

sections.heading: 4. Calculate income after costs
sections.body:
Suppose a sample apartment requires AED 1,200,000 in total acquisition cost. Assume AED 80,000 annual rent, AED 8,000 vacancy allowance and AED 18,000 of owner costs. Net operating income is AED 54,000, or 4.5% of the total cost, before finance, tax and sale costs. These example figures show how rent and annual costs combine in a yield calculation.

The chart shows the rent, deductions and resulting income as parts of one calculation. Use recent signed leases for similar units, including size, condition, parking, view and furnishing. Compare asking rents with signed leases and the income collected from similar homes.

Test a longer vacancy and higher repair or service charge. A view may help tenant appeal, but its effect on rent must be supported by comparable evidence.

chart.title: Example waterfront rental calculation
chart.note: Sample figures; net income equals rent less deductions and excludes finance, tax and sale costs.

sections.heading: 5. Check insurance, access and intended use
sections.body:
Ask the insurer what risks and parts of the property are covered, what exclusions apply and how claims are handled. Review the building's rules for balconies, pets, alterations and access to shared facilities. A sea view does not necessarily mean private beach access or an included berth.

If you intend short-term accommodation, confirm the current licensing and building requirements with the relevant Sharjah authorities before assuming that use is permitted. A long-term residential lease has different obligations.

Visit the building at the times a tenant might use it and test parking and travel to work or services. A convenient promenade does not automatically make every daily journey convenient.

sections.heading: 6. Assess the exit and downside
sections.body:
Look for recent completed sales of similar units and separate them from asking prices. Record the floor, view, size, condition and tenancy so differences are visible. Include selling expenses and any outstanding loan in an eventual proceeds estimate.

Test a lower sale price, longer vacancy and an unexpected repair. Keep a cash reserve and do not rely on a forecast of appreciation to meet a contractual payment. If the comparable evidence is thin, use a range and seek a suitable professional valuation.

Keep the evidence dated and update it if the market, building condition or financing changes. A past sale can inform a range, but it does not ensure that a new buyer will pay the same amount or that a sale will complete within a particular period.

sections.heading: Request current waterfront options
sections.body:
Browse [Aliyas Maryam Island projects](/projects?emirate=Sharjah&area=sharjah-maryam-island) and [Al Khan projects](/projects?emirate=Sharjah&area=sharjah-al-khan). [Contact Aliyas](/contact) with your budget, nationality and intended use.

Ask which units are currently available and request the exact plan, ownership documents and current charges. Compare the evidence for each specific home. Verify the property and official requirements before committing.

aliyas-journal-166.excerpt: Compare Sharjah areas for Dubai commuters using the actual door-to-door journey, housing and transport costs, and household needs.
aliyas-journal-166.introduction:
The best Sharjah area for a Dubai commuter depends on the workplace, departure time and exact building. A home near the border may still involve a long route to a particular office, while a cheaper rent can be offset by fuel, parking or a second car. Test the complete journey before signing.

Al Nahda Sharjah, Al Taawun and Muwaileh are starting points for a search, not a universal ranking. The cost example shows how rent and commuting expenses can be compared across two homes.
takeaways: Measure the full journey from the apartment door to the actual workplace and back.
Compare rent and transport costs together, while accounting for school and other household trips.
Check the current lease, utility and transport terms for the specific home.

sections.heading: Where should a commuter start looking?
sections.body:
[Bayut's Al Nahda Sharjah guide](https://www.bayut.com/area-guides/al-nahda-sharjah/) describes an apartment area on the Dubai–Sharjah border; it should not be confused with Al Nahda in Dubai. Its [Al Taawun guide](https://www.bayut.com/area-guides/al-taawun/) describes a tower district near the border, while [Muwaileh](https://www.bayut.com/area-guides/muwaileh/) offers another residential search area. Test the journey from the building entrance at the times you expect to travel.

Record the actual entrance, parking and road access. If commuting by public transport, include the trip to a stop, waiting, transfers and the final leg to work. Visit on a working day at the time you would travel.

The [Al Majaz and Al Taawun family rental guide](/journal/al-majaz-vs-al-taawun-family-rental-comparison) offers further building and household checks.

table.caption: Commuter shortlist questions
rows: Exact building and crossing into the required Dubai route
Tower access, parking and the actual work destination
Building, road entry and school or work journeys
Door-to-door time, transport costs and lease terms

sections.heading: Check current transport rather than a map alone
sections.body:
Dubai RTA's [timetable page](https://rta.ae/wps/portal/rta/ae/public-transport/timetable) lists intercity bus services, while [Sharjah RTA's intercity schedule](https://www.srta.gov.ae/en-us/TransportServices/Intercity-Bus-Schedule.html) provides a route and timetable lookup. Verify current stops, hours and fares for the actual journey before relying on a bus.

Include the first and final legs, the wait at a station and the return trip. If driving, record fuel, tolls, parking and maintenance. Test the route more than once; a single quiet day is not a reliable average.

Ask whether work permits flexible hours or remote days. A change in office attendance can materially change the annual cost and time spent travelling.

sections.heading: Compare rent and transport together
sections.body:
Imagine option A costs AED 65,000 in annual rent and AED 16,000 in transport, while option B costs AED 58,000 in rent and AED 26,000 in transport. Their combined amounts are AED 81,000 and AED 84,000. The example applies the same calculation to each of the two rental options.

The chart compares those two totals only. Add utilities, cooling, parking, school transport and non-refundable lease charges where they differ. A lower annual cost is not automatically the best choice if the journey or apartment fails your requirements.

Treat refundable deposits separately as move-in cash, and put all rent instalments on a calendar. Confirm every amount and date in the written agreement.

chart.title: Example annual rent plus transport
chart.note: Example inputs compare the combined annual costs of the two rental options.

sections.heading: Inspect the home and its building
sections.body:
Check bedroom layout, storage, cooling, water pressure, windows and visible condition. Confirm the allocated parking and the route from it to the lift. Ask whether cooling and utilities are included, who pays for repairs and how faults are reported.

Visit shared areas and check lifts, entry controls and any facility the household expects to use. If the home is furnished, agree the inventory and condition. Inspect the apartment and compare its layout and view with the property details.

For families, ask schools about places and transport for the exact address. Test the combined school and work route, not only a direct home-to-office trip.

sections.heading: Review the Sharjah lease
sections.body:
Ask for the annual rent, payment dates, deposit, non-refundable fees, maintenance, renewal and early-exit terms. Verify the landlord's or representative's authority and the payment recipient. Record the apartment's condition at handover and retain receipts.

Sharjah Municipality's [residential tenancy contract template](https://portal.shjmun.gov.ae/en/eservices/Attachements/Residential-Tenancy-Contract-Template.pdf) describes attestation and party obligations under the referenced law. Confirm the current process, deadline and charges with the municipality for the actual agreement.

Ask how utility accounts are opened and whether existing balances are settled. A refundable deposit affects the cash needed at move-in even if it is later returned.

sections.heading: Assess the household's full week
sections.body:
List office days, school trips, activities and journeys by other household members. A short commute for one person may require a longer trip for another. Check whether a second car is needed and whether nearby services are accessible to someone without one.

Set a maximum acceptable door-to-door time and a total annual housing and transport budget. Leave room for changes in fuel, rent or working patterns. Compare observations for each actual home rather than assuming the whole area has one experience.

sections.heading: Put the travel time in perspective
sections.body:
For illustration, a journey that is thirty minutes longer in each direction adds one hour on a commuting day. At five days a week for 48 weeks, that is 240 hours in a year. The calculation shows how travel time can be considered alongside the household budget.

Decide how that time affects your family routine and whether flexible hours change the calculation. Avoid treating a chosen value for your time as a cash payment unless it actually changes income or expenses. Record the time separately from rent and transport so both can inform the decision without creating a misleading total.

sections.heading: Request current rental options
sections.body:
Browse the [Aliyas Sharjah project collection](/projects?emirate=Sharjah) for local context and ask which relevant rental homes are currently available. Request the current lease terms for the home that fits your preferred commute.

[Contact Aliyas](/contact) with your workplace, preferred bedrooms and budget. Request the exact address and written terms, then test the journey and view the apartment.
