aliyas-journal-198.excerpt: Understand the UAE property investor Golden Residency criteria, supporting documents and route-specific fees using official ICP guidance.
aliyas-journal-198.introduction:
Property investment may provide a route to UAE Golden Residency when the applicant and property meet the applicable conditions. The published criteria and required documents depend on the application route and can change. Buying a property does not automatically grant a visa.

This guide summarises official ICP information checked on 8 November 2026. Confirm current eligibility, documentation and costs with the authority handling your application before committing.
takeaways: ICP's real estate investment guidance states an AED 2 million property-value threshold subject to conditions.
Financed and off-plan cases require the authority to confirm the applicable route and evidence.
An entry-permit fee is only one part of a residency application, not the total cost.

sections.heading: What is the property investment threshold?
sections.body:
[ICP's Golden Residency guide](https://icp.gov.ae/en/services/uae-golden-residency/) describes a 10-year residency category for qualifying real estate investors. It states that the investor must own one or more UAE properties with a total value of at least AED 2 million, with full ownership registered in the investor's name. It also describes a route for qualifying off-plan units of at least AED 2 million purchased from an approved local real estate company.

The authority determines eligibility and supporting evidence for the applicant. Ask how value, ownership shares and the specific property are assessed before treating any purchase as qualifying. The threshold is one eligibility condition, with approval determined through the relevant application process.

table.caption: Application preparation checklist
rows: Eligible value, valuation evidence and ownership share
Registration, approved developer and applicable route
Lender, mortgage and payment evidence requirements
Entry, residency, ID, medical, insurance and service charges

sections.heading: Can a financed property qualify?
sections.body:
The ICP guide says a property may be financed through a loan from an approved local bank, subject to its stated conditions. However, the relevant service and local application channel can require specific evidence. [ICP's residency permit service](https://icp.gov.ae/en/services-details/?serviceid=64afe3c1035448005bd52e64) lists property valuation or mortgaged-title evidence among the documents for applicable categories.

Ask the authority handling your application how a mortgage, outstanding balance, payments and valuation affect your particular case. Do not assume any deposit or lender automatically satisfies every route. Obtain the bank's documents and a written explanation of the current requirement before relying on residency when choosing a property.

sections.heading: What about off-plan property?
sections.body:
The ICP guide describes an off-plan route where qualifying units total at least AED 2 million and the purchase is from an approved local real estate company authorised by the competent local authority. Check that the named developer, project, unit and registration meet the current conditions. A sales brochure is not an eligibility decision.

Ask whether the authority requires an interim registration, valuation, payment evidence or other documents for your circumstances. Confirm the impact of construction status and any financing. If the application depends on a future handover or registration, include that timing in your plan and do not represent the residency as already approved.

sections.heading: Which documents should you prepare?
sections.body:
The [ICP real estate investor entry-permit service](https://icp.gov.ae/en/services-details/?serviceid=68e34eea5ae59b00117383d5) lists a passport, personal photograph and a letter from the real estate registration department confirming qualifying ownership. The service also lists a passport valid for at least six months and valid UAE health insurance among its conditions. The exact checklist depends on the service, applicant and current rules.

Prepare the title or relevant registration, valuation and financing documents requested by the authority. Ask about translations, attestation and family documents before submitting. Submit personal records through an official application channel and retain copies of the documents you provide.

sections.heading: How much does the entry permit cost?
sections.body:
As checked on 8 November 2026, ICP's entry-permit service lists AED 100 application, AED 100 issuance and AED 100 smart-services fees: AED 300 for those listed items. This is the entry-permit service only, not the complete Golden Residency, Emirates ID or family cost. It may not apply in the same way to every applicant.

Additional charges can include residency issuance, identification, medical screening, insurance, valuation, translation or assistance, depending on the route and applicant. Obtain an itemised current quote from ICP or the relevant authorised channel. Do not combine unrelated fees into a claimed universal total.

chart.title: ICP entry-permit service fees listed at review
chart.note: ICP listing checked 8 November 2026. AED 300 covers these entry-permit items only; other residency costs are excluded.

sections.heading: How does the application process work?
sections.body:
The entry-permit service describes submission through ICP's smart services or app, review of the form, attachment of documents if required, payment and receipt of the outcome. Its role is to allow an eligible investor to complete the residency process; it is not itself proof that the full residence permit has been issued.

The residency permit is a separate process and may be linked to an Emirates ID application. Ask the authority which steps apply to your current location and visa status, what medical or insurance conditions apply and how to track the application. Processing times and requirements can change.

sections.heading: What about family members and continuing conditions?
sections.body:
ICP's Golden Residency guide describes benefits for eligible family members and health insurance requirements. Ask the authority about each dependant's eligibility, supporting documents, insurance, fees and the period of the residence permit. Do not assume the main applicant's property paperwork automatically completes a family application.

Keep property and insurance records current and ask the authority about renewal, changes in ownership or financing and any reporting obligations. Eligibility is assessed under the rules applicable at the time; a property purchase should also make financial sense independently of the visa outcome.

sections.heading: Check the property itself
sections.body:
Residency eligibility is separate from the right to buy a specific property. Confirm the buyer's legal right, seller authority, project or title registration, purchase costs and payment instructions with the relevant land authority. Review the complete contract and financing obligations.

The [Dubai property buyer guide](/journal/how-to-buy-property-in-dubai-as-a-non-resident) and [Abu Dhabi area guide](/journal/abu-dhabi-real-estate-2026) provide location context. Neither replaces a decision by ICP, a local land authority or a lender.

sections.heading: Request current information
sections.body:
Browse [Aliyas UAE projects](/projects) and [contact Aliyas](/contact) with your budget and intended location. Ask for current units and ownership documents, then independently confirm the Golden Residency route, value, evidence and all fees with the responsible authority.

Before publication or an application, recheck the official pages because rules and service charges can change. Obtain professional advice for a complex ownership or immigration case.

aliyas-journal-199.excerpt: Calculate UAE property cash flow after vacancy, operating costs, debt payments and a planned capital reserve.
aliyas-journal-199.introduction:
Property cash flow is the money left after the relevant income and expenses actually fall due. It differs from gross rental yield and from a gain on a future sale. Calculate it with the signed lease, the building's charges and the real financing schedule, then test a less favourable year.

The example below shows how rent, expenses and financing come together in one cash-flow calculation.
takeaways: Separate potential rent, vacancy, operating costs, debt service and capital spending.
A positive operating yield can coexist with negative cash flow after loan payments.
Use actual dates and written costs, and stress-test vacancy and repairs.

sections.heading: What is the cash-flow formula?
sections.body:
Start with potential annual rent, subtract a vacancy or non-collection allowance, then subtract owner-paid operating expenses. The result is net operating income. Subtract annual mortgage payments and planned capital spending to estimate cash flow before tax and sale. State exactly which costs are included, so the calculation can be compared with another property.

For example: AED 80,000 potential rent minus AED 5,000 vacancy and AED 20,000 operating expenses gives AED 55,000 net operating income. Minus AED 36,000 debt payments and AED 5,000 planned capital spending leaves AED 14,000 annual cash flow. These are sample numbers.

table.caption: Sample annual calculation
rows: Cash flow before tax and sale

chart.title: Example annual income and outflows
chart.note: Sample amounts; cash remaining is after the listed deductions, before tax and sale.

sections.heading: Use rent you can support with evidence
sections.body:
For an existing tenancy, start with the signed lease and the payment schedule. For a vacant home, seek recent signed leases of similar units, noting the building, area, condition, furnishing and date. An asking rent is not necessarily collected rent. Distinguish an annual rent paid in instalments from cash actually received in each month.

Allow for time between tenants and the possibility of delayed or unpaid rent. The example's AED 5,000 vacancy allowance is a sample assumption, not a UAE average. Ask a local manager for documented comparables and vary the assumption to see how the result changes.

sections.heading: Include operating costs
sections.body:
Request the actual service-charge statement, insurance quote and management agreement. Add owner-paid repairs, maintenance, utilities during vacancy and other recurring costs. If the tenant pays a particular utility or service directly, do not also deduct it from the owner's cash flow. Separate a refundable security deposit held for a tenant from rental income.

For short stays, check current permits and building rules and include cleaning, linen, platform charges, utilities and operator fees. Confirm the fee base and whether it applies to gross bookings or net receipts. Use evidence for the specific strategy and property.

sections.heading: Distinguish finance and capital costs
sections.body:
A mortgage payment commonly includes principal and interest or profit. Both are cash outflows, while principal repayment reduces the outstanding loan; do not treat the whole payment as an operating expense when calculating net operating income. Use the bank's actual schedule and include insurance and fees in the appropriate period.

A planned replacement of furniture, cooling equipment or another major item is a capital cash need. In the example, AED 5,000 is a planning allowance rather than proof that a repair will cost that amount. Record actual spending when it occurs and avoid deducting the same expense twice.

sections.heading: Compare yield and cash on cash
sections.body:
Gross yield is annual rent divided by property price, without operating deductions. Net operating yield is net operating income divided by the chosen cost basis. Cash-on-cash return compares cash flow with the buyer's cash invested, but only if all relevant cash inputs and the period are clearly defined. None of these measures guarantees future income or resale value.

If the worked example used AED 400,000 of the buyer's cash, AED 14,000 divided by AED 400,000 would equal 3.5% before tax and sale. The denominator must include the buyer's actual deposit and purchase expenses; this is not a quoted market return.

sections.heading: Stress-test a difficult year
sections.body:
Increase vacancy, add a repair and change the mortgage rate using the lender's actual reset formula. If the AED 80,000 example loses another AED 10,000 of rent and incurs AED 8,000 of extra repairs, the AED 14,000 cash flow becomes negative AED 4,000 before tax and sale, assuming other items are unchanged. Keep a reserve for such periods.

The [Central Bank’s 2024 financial stability report](https://www.centralbank.ae/media/p2rpafum/cbuae-fsr-report_2025_en.pdf) describes lender affordability requirements. A lender's approval does not remove the owner's need to budget for vacancies, maintenance and changing rates.

sections.heading: Build a monthly calendar
sections.body:
Annual totals can hide a cash shortage when service charges, insurance or loan payments fall before rent is received. Map each due date and receipt on a monthly calendar, including large repairs and any developer instalments. A monthly calendar shows when payments and income fall due across the year.

The [Dubai Land Department tenancy registration service](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/register-renew-ejari-contract/) describes an official Dubai process; verify the current registration requirements for the property and other emirates locally. Use the lease and bank statements to reconcile planned against actual cash.

sections.heading: Account for the purchase and sale
sections.body:
The operating calculation begins after acquisition and does not include the initial price, transfer fees or furnishing. Record those cash outflows separately when measuring total performance. If the apartment is sold, include the sale proceeds, brokerage and other selling costs, and repay any outstanding mortgage. Do not add the entire sale price to annual rent or count repayment of principal twice.

If you intend to compare several years, record when each amount is received or paid and use the same assumptions for each property. A professional can help assess tax treatment and a more detailed return calculation. Keep the basic monthly cash forecast separate from an uncertain future sale price.

sections.heading: Apply the calculation to current homes
sections.body:
Use the [Dubai rental yield guide](/journal/how-to-calculate-net-rental-yield-in-dubai) and [Ajman area guide](/journal/ajman-property-2026) for related context. Browse [Aliyas UAE projects](/projects) and [contact Aliyas](/contact) for current units, then request actual charges, lease evidence and financing terms.

Update the model whenever a quote, vacancy or rate changes. Seek tax or accounting advice where relevant to your circumstances.

aliyas-journal-200.excerpt: Review the fees, authority, reporting, maintenance and exit clauses in a UAE property management agreement before appointing a landlord's manager.
aliyas-journal-200.introduction:
A property management agreement determines what the manager will do, how the landlord pays and who can make decisions about the home. A low advertised fee is only useful if the scope, other charges, reporting and authority limits are clear.

Review the contract for the exact property and intended rental strategy, and verify the manager's credentials with the responsible local authority.
takeaways: Define the services, fee basis and payment handling in writing.
Set repair approval limits, reporting, insurance and tenant communication responsibilities.
Check the duration, termination process and transfer of keys, deposits and records.

sections.heading: Define the manager's scope
sections.body:
List who markets the home, arranges viewings, screens tenants, prepares the lease, handles registration, collects rent and manages renewals. Specify whether inspections, move-in and move-out reports, rent collection and emergency attendance are included. A leasing-only service and ongoing management may have different scopes.

For Dubai, [DLD's licensed brokers service](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/licensed-real-estate-brokers/?r=1) provides a way to check licensed brokers. Verify the manager’s company and authorisation for the relevant property management activity with the competent authority.

table.caption: Agreement checklist
rows: Percentage base, fixed charges, tax and third-party costs
Repair approval, emergencies and spending limits
Rent, tenant deposits, account and payout schedule
Notice, termination fees, records and keys

sections.heading: Compare the real cost of management
sections.body:
Ask whether the fee is based on rent due, rent collected or another amount, and whether VAT applies. Request separate charges for finding a tenant, renewal, advertising, inspection, call-outs and administration. Check whether contractor invoices include a management markup and who must approve it.

Imagine AED 80,000 collected rent and a sample 5% management fee based on that amount: AED 4,000 before any applicable tax or additional charges. At a sample 8%, the fee would be AED 6,400. These are arithmetic examples, not standard UAE fees or current quotations.

chart.title: Sample annual management fee
chart.note: Sample AED 80,000 rent and fee rates; excludes tax and additional services.

sections.heading: Control rent and deposits
sections.body:
Specify which account receives rent, when the manager transfers the landlord's share and how a statement reconciles income and deductions. Ask for invoices and receipts and establish who can authorise refunds. The agreement should explain how tenant deposits are held, documented and returned under the applicable rules.

Do not treat a refundable tenant deposit as rental income. Confirm what happens if rent is late or a payment fails, who communicates with the tenant and when the landlord must approve further action. Verify bank details independently and keep a record of each payment.

sections.heading: Set maintenance authority
sections.body:
Agree a spending limit for routine repairs and what constitutes an emergency. Specify how the manager contacts the owner, what happens if the owner cannot be reached and whether the limit applies per job or over a defined period. Request photographs, quotations, invoices and proof of completed work.

Ask how contractors are selected, whether the manager receives commissions and whether the owner can use a preferred contractor. Clarify responsibility for tenant-caused damage, warranty claims and common-area faults. An emergency provision should not become unlimited authority for unrelated improvements.

sections.heading: Review tenant and legal processes
sections.body:
Identify who prepares the lease, checks tenant documents, conducts inspections and registers or renews the tenancy where required. The [Dubai Land Department tenancy registration service](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/register-renew-ejari-contract/) describes a Dubai process; check the current rules and authority in other emirates. The manager should not promise an outcome in a dispute.

If short stays are intended, verify the relevant local permit, building rules, guest handling, cleaning, platform fees and insurance before appointing an operator. A long-term management contract may not cover holiday-home activity.

sections.heading: Agree reporting and insurance
sections.body:
Set a reporting frequency and require a statement showing rent received, vacancy, deductions, maintenance, deposit movements and amounts paid to the owner. Agree how the owner can see supporting documents and how long records are retained. Ask how tenant and owner information will be protected and who may access it.

Confirm the building's policy and the owner's separate insurance needs. Check whether the manager holds any relevant cover and what it excludes. Insurance terms depend on the policy and do not automatically cover every loss or vacancy.

sections.heading: Read the exit provisions
sections.body:
Check the contract term, renewal, notice period, termination fee and circumstances in which either party may end it. Specify the handover of keys, tenant contacts, lease, deposits, maintenance history and outstanding rent. Ask how unpaid invoices or disputes will be reconciled.

If the property is sold, agree what happens to an existing tenant and the manager's authority. Ensure the owner can obtain records promptly and that no continuing marketing or payment authority survives beyond what was agreed. Seek legal advice if a clause is unclear.

sections.heading: Test the agreement against a real scenario
sections.body:
Ask the prospective manager to walk through a vacant month, an urgent repair and a tenant renewal. Request a sample statement and a written fee schedule. Compare several proposals on scope and controls, not only the percentage shown in an advertisement.

Ask who will communicate with the tenant outside normal office hours and whether the owner receives a copy of correspondence. Check the target response time, how missed payments are reported and whether legal proceedings require a separate appointment. These details make the difference between a service description and a workable arrangement. The agreement should reflect the property's actual use and the owner's availability.

sections.heading: Start with the property and its requirements
sections.body:
Use the [Ajman area guide](/journal/ajman-property-2026) and [RAK lifestyle guide](/journal/ras-al-khaimah-property-lifestyle) for local context. Browse [Aliyas UAE projects](/projects) and [contact Aliyas](/contact) for current property information. Verify the manager, local requirements and the agreement before signing.

For an existing lease, ask how the manager will obtain the contract, tenant deposit record, keys and maintenance history. Agree the opening balance and any work already authorised. Retain a copy of the signed agreement and check the first statement against the bank and the supporting invoices.
